Progress is layered by resets: augmentations bought with money and faction reputation (each purchase doubling later prices) take effect only when installed, which wipes most progress, and destroying a BitNode by hacking w0r1d_d43m0n at hacking level 3000 resets further but grants a permanent Source-File. This prestige-reset structure has no taxonomy entry, so this run proposed one. Later BitNodes add systems such as Bladeburner and sleeves.

mechanics.note: Netscript scripts in JavaScript run on servers whose RAM caps how many threads can run; the TIX API automates stock trading, and a beginner path teaches programming from scratch.

hack() takes a share of a server's finite money that rises with hacking level and falls with security; grow() restores money and weaken() lowers security toward its floor, and both hack and grow raise security, so sustained yield needs a balanced hack-grow-weaken schedule.
Working for factions builds reputation that gates which augmentations can be bought; Daedalus reputation gates The Red Pill needed to end a BitNode.
Hacking, combat, and charisma stats rise with use; hacking level raises success chance and money stolen, shortens hack time, and gates which servers can be hacked.
Stock prices move about every 6 seconds by a forecast probability that large trades shift; hacking or growing a company's server can lower or raise its stock's hidden forecast.
Coding contracts found on servers pose programming problems that earn rewards when solved.
Time spent offline accumulates and later speeds stock-market updates from about every 6 seconds to about every 4.
Each script has a RAM cost, and a server's RAM caps how many script threads can run on it, so buying RAM and writing lean scripts both raise income.

games.name: Bitburner
games.summary: A free, open-source incremental hacking game in which the player writes JavaScript scripts that hack, grow, and weaken simulated servers for money, then spends it with faction reputation on augmentations that reset progress in exchange for permanent multipliers.

games.core_loop: impress villagers with miracles, help, or fear -> belief grows and worship generates prayer power -> cast miracles with the Hand and gestures -> train the creature with strokes and slaps -> the creature acts on learned desires -> convert rival villages and move to the next island
games.design_notes: Richard Evans built the creature on a belief-desire-intention model after Bratman: beliefs are lists of data about world objects, desires are simplified perceptrons, and opinions are decision trees about how to satisfy a desire; the creature picks the belief with the best opinion for each desire as its intention, and strokes and slaps adjust those opinions by reinforcement. A leash directs the creature's attention so it can learn by observation. The player's actions also move a good-evil alignment that changes the land, interface, music, and followers' view of the god, with a good and an evil advisor arguing each case; alignment has no mechanic id yet (proposal filed). The interface is an animated hand that throws objects and casts gestures instead of icons and panels.

mechanics.note: The creature forms intentions from a belief-desire-intention model with perceptron desires and decision-tree opinions; stroking rewards and slapping discourages the last action, the creature remembers and generalizes these responses, and a leash focuses it on actions the player demonstrates.

Miracles such as food, wood, healing, shields, fireballs, and lightning are cast from the Temple or Village Centre or by drawing gestures with the Hand, powered by villagers' worship, sacrifices, or one-shot Miracle Dispensers.
Each villager holds a belief level in the player's god, raised by help or intimidation; villagers tire of repeated tactics, and a village converts when enough believe.
The creature must be fed and taught what and when to eat, and it grows over the game.
Villagers need food, healing, and rest before they will worship.
A good and an evil advisor push the player toward each alignment.
Buildings are placed from Workshop blueprints and built by villagers.
Villagers gather wood and food, for example by fishing.
Real local weather can be imported.

games.name: Black & White
games.summary: A god game in which the player wins villagers' belief through miracles, help, or fear while training a giant creature whose behavior is learned from the player's rewards and punishments.

games.core_loop: place housing plots and roads -> walkers from service buildings roam the roads and cover the houses they pass -> houses evolve when food, goods, and services reach them -> taxes and trade fund the city -> raise culture, prosperity, peace, and favor ratings to win the mission
games.design_notes: Coverage is delivered by individual walkers whose routes depend on road layout, so the same buildings serve a block well or badly depending on junctions; the developers cited SimCity's static placement as what they wanted to make less static. In the logic preserved by the Julius re-implementation, a walker sets a house's coverage to 96 and coverage decays by 1 per update, while prefects zero fire risk and engineers zero collapse risk. City and empire share one map, and gods that punish neglect have no matching taxonomy mechanic (see run proposal).

mechanics.note: Service walkers leave their building and roam roads; each house passed gets coverage set to 96, which decays by 1 per update until the next visit.
Housing evolves through levels from tents up to villas and palaces when food, goods, services, and desirability are met, and devolves when they lapse.
Each assignment sets population and thresholds for four ratings: culture, prosperity, peace, and favor.
Higher houses need food plus pottery, furniture, oil, and wine delivered by market walkers.
Raw materials such as clay, olives, and timber become pottery, oil, and furniture in workshops.
An empire map opens land and sea routes to cities that buy and sell specific goods.
Buildings accumulate fire and collapse risk that prefects and engineers reset to zero.
Favor with Caesar rises with timely tribute and gifts and falls when requests are missed.
Military assignments bring invasions; legions, walls, and towers defend the city map.
Buildings need workers from housing; shortages idle walkers and industry.
Gardens, statues, and plazas raise desirability that houses need to evolve.
Walkers and goods move on roads, so road layout sets coverage.

games.name: Caesar III
games.summary: A Roman city builder in which service walkers roam the roads from their buildings, houses evolve only where food, goods, and services actually reach them, and missions are won on culture, prosperity, peace, and favor ratings.

games.core_loop: buy land and place a firm -> lay out its internal units -> link purchasing, manufacturing, and sales units into supply chains -> set prices and advertising -> compete for market share on price, quality, and brand -> reinvest, research, or trade stock
games.design_notes: Trevor Chan's Capitalism models a firm as a small grid of internal units (purchasing, manufacturing, sales, advertising) that the player wires together, so every factory, farm, mine, and store is a layout and logistics puzzle inside a market model. Retail is the main income source: each department store sells up to four products, and customers weigh price, product quality, and brand against competing stores. R&D centers raise product quality over projects lasting from six months to ten years, and AI rivals can be set from aggressive to conservative. An optional stock market allows takeovers, and hired presidents can run divisions. Advertising spend that builds brand awareness has no mechanic in the taxonomy (proposed as advertising-awareness).

mechanics.note: Factories turn purchased inputs into products through linked manufacturing units; farms, mines, oil wells, and logging camps supply raw materials.
City consumers pick among stores by price, product quality, and brand; each department store stocks up to four items.
AI corporations with aggressive to conservative management styles compete in the same cities for market share.
Each firm is a grid of internal units placed and linked by the player; layout decides what flows where.
Product quality comes from input quality and technology level and drives demand and price.
R&D centers run projects from six months to ten years that raise technology and unlock new products.
An optional stock market lets the player buy shares, take over rivals, or be bought out.
Mines, oil wells, farms, and logging camps produce raw materials.
Hired presidents can run divisions day to day.
A layout plan library saves and reuses firm unit layouts.
Seventeen scenarios set goals such as market-share dominance within a time limit.
Advertising units inside firms spend money to raise a product's brand rating, which customers weigh with price and quality when choosing among stores.

games.name: Capitalism
games.summary: A corporate business sim in which the player builds retail stores, factories, farms, mines, and R&D centers from internal unit layouts and competes with AI firms on price, quality, and brand across city markets.

claims.text: Captain of Industry entered Steam Early Access on 2022-05-31 and was still in Early Access in October 2026, with the developers estimating two to four more years.

games.core_loop: designate mining and dumping areas -> trucks haul ore and rock -> smelt and refine into goods -> feed, power, and house the population -> satisfied needs generate Unity -> spend Unity and products on research, edicts, and ship expeditions -> expand and terraform
games.design_notes: Captain of Industry joins a factory game to a settlement whose population is both labor and a consumer: residents need housing, food, water, electricity, healthcare, and household goods, each fully satisfied need yields about one to two Unity per month, and Unity buys edicts, outposts, quick trades, instant construction, and emergency repairs. Every working vehicle and many buildings consume crafted Maintenance I, II, or III; below 75% a monthly breakdown roll begins, reaching 50% at zero, so maintenance is itself a production chain whose failure cascades through the economy. Terrain is a stock of materials: excavators dig inside a Mine Control Tower's area, trucks dump rock and dirt that settle at per-material angles of repose (about 42 degrees for loose dirt to 78 for hardened rock), and dumping reclaims ocean for ports. A ship explores a world map for islands, refugees, and trade partners. Unity works like a political-capital currency earned from welfare, which the taxonomy lacks; this run proposed one.

mechanics.note: Smelters, refineries, chemical plants, food processors, and assembly lines run recipe chains from iron and copper ore to electronics, fuel, consumer goods, and nuclear fuel across 100+ technologies.
Trucks are assigned to mines, storages, and buildings and automatically deliver products where they are needed, so fleet size and road layout cap throughput before belts and trains replace them.

Mining designations inside a Mine Control Tower area lower terrain and dumping designations raise it; loose material settles at per-material angles of repose, retaining walls stabilize slopes, and dumping can reclaim ocean.
Residents consume food, water, electricity, healthcare, and household goods; each fully satisfied need yields Unity, and unmet food or health shrinks the population.
Working vehicles and buildings consume Maintenance I to III crafted at depots (idle at about a third); below 75% maintenance a breakdown is rolled monthly with chance rising to 50% at zero.
Excavators dig ore, coal, limestone, and rock from designated terrain, while oil rigs, quartz and uranium mines, and water pumps work fixed deposits and outposts.
The player paints mining and dumping designations, and excavators and trucks assigned to a Mine Control Tower carry out the work inside its area.
Belts and pipes give high-throughput direct links between machines once truck logistics become a bottleneck.
Generators up to nuclear reactors feed the settlement and factories, and residents require electricity as one of their needs.
Research labs consume products and Unity to unlock over 100 technologies from basic smelting to space flight.
Air and water pollution and unmanaged waste spread disease among the population.
Production emits slag, waste, carbon dioxide, wastewater, and spent nuclear fuel that must be dumped, treated, recycled, or stored.
Captain's Office edicts change settlement rules, such as raising population growth by tier, for a monthly Unity cost.
Ships explore a world map to discover islands and trading partners; quick trades and recurring contracts exchange goods.
Farms grow crops for food and industrial inputs, fertilizer boosts yields, and greenhouses grow advanced crops.
Storages and loose storage piles buffer materials, and full outputs stall production upstream.
Trains move bulk cargo over long distances, and ships run trade contracts between the home island and partners.
Unity income, population change, edict costs, and maintenance breakdown rolls resolve monthly.
Each fully satisfied settlement need yields about 1 to 2 Unity per month, spent on edicts, outposts, quick trades, instant construction, and emergency repairs.
Unity is spent on building boosts (0.25 Unity each) that speed up individual buildings.

games.name: Captain of Industry
games.summary: An industrial colony builder in which the player reshapes island terrain with excavators and trucks, runs production chains to feed, house, and power a settlement, and spends the Unity its satisfied population generates on edicts, quick builds, and world-map expansion.

games.core_loop: accept a generated customer order -> inspect and test the car -> remove parts in order to reach faulty ones -> buy or repair replacements -> reassemble and test drive -> get paid -> upgrade the garage and restore cars for sale
games.design_notes: The car is a tree of modeled parts (over 4000 across 72 cars) with a removal order, so labor is spent reaching a faulty component before replacing it, the series loop carried over from Car Mechanic Simulator 2018. Customer orders are generated without end, while story missions, car and salvage auctions, barn finds, and a project-car restoration supply variety. A skills and garage-upgrade system gates faster or more capable work.

mechanics.note: Orders list symptoms; the player examines engine, suspension, and chassis, removes covering parts in a realistic order to reach damaged ones, replaces or repairs them, and verifies the fix, across over 4000 parts on 72 cars.
An endless supply of generated customer orders plus story missions with their own requirements provide income.
Car auctions and salvage auctions supply restoration projects for resale.
Experience feeds a skills and garage-upgrade system.
Repaired and tuned cars can be driven, including time trials on a race track.

games.name: Car Mechanic Simulator 2021
games.summary: A first-person garage sim in which the player diagnoses and repairs customer cars part by part, restores auction and barn-find cars, and expands the workshop.

claims.text: Early access began 2015-07-15 and 1.0 released 2024-12-05, published by Kitfox Games.
Caves of Qud is among the shipped games listed as using wave function collapse.

games.core_loop: explore generated and handmade zones -> fight, trade, and talk with faction members -> mutate and equip -> uncover generated history -> go deeper
games.design_notes: A roguelike included for its simulation layers: faction reputation that every creature carries, liquids that mix and flow, body-part anatomy, and procedurally generated sultan histories that the world refers to. It is a frequently cited example of wave function collapse in a shipped game.

mechanics.note: Every creature belongs to factions; the player's standing with each faction decides who attacks, trades, or talks.
Generated histories of past sultans are written into the world as lore, shrines, and quests.
Zones mix handmade and procedural maps; some generators use wave function collapse.

games.name: Caves of Qud
games.summary: A science-fantasy roguelike RPG with simulated factions, liquids, body parts, and procedurally generated histories, built partly with wave function collapse.

claims.text: Cities: Skylines is credited with reviving the SimCity style of city builder after SimCity (2013).

games.core_loop: draw roads and zone along them -> citizens move in, commute, and shop along computed routes -> population milestones unlock services and map tiles -> set district policies, taxes, and budgets -> fix traffic with road hierarchy and transit -> expand
games.design_notes: Colossal Order carried the road and transit systems of its Cities in Motion series into a full city builder, so every citizen and vehicle is an agent taking the fastest route and congestion is read directly from visible jams. Zoning cells are generated along whatever road geometry the player draws, freeing layouts from a fixed grid, and districts let the player apply policies and tax rates to painted areas. Paradox approved the project after the reception of SimCity (2013), the game was built for Steam Workshop mods, and widely used mods replace core systems such as traffic rules.

mechanics.note: Zoning cells follow the shape of drawn roads; residential, commercial, industrial, and office zones develop and level up.
Road type sets lanes, speed, and zone frontage; network geometry such as interchanges and one-way systems decides throughput.
Each citizen takes the fastest route to work or other destinations; poor road design shows up as visible jams that delay services and deliveries.
Player-drawn bus, tram, train, metro, ferry, and taxi lines carry passengers, cut congestion, and earn fares.
Citizens and vehicles path individually through roads, paths, and transit.
Population milestones unlock services, zoning types, policies, and purchase of up to 25 map tiles.
District policies restrict development types, set district tax rates, or make transit free.
Water and sewage pipes; sewage released upstream contaminates downstream intakes.
Service buildings reach buildings by network distance and dispatch vehicles.
Elementary (300), high school (1,000), and university (4,500) capacities move citizens through four education levels that higher-level jobs require.
Citizens age and die; an initial cohort moving in together can age into a wave of deaths that overloads hearses.
Services and parks raise land value, pollution and noise lower it, and land value helps buildings level up.
Steam Workshop and a mod-friendly architecture; mods add assets, maps, and new behavior.
Citizens choose between walking, driving, and the player's bus, tram, train, metro, ferry, and taxi lines when routing to destinations, so new lines shift demand off roads.

games.name: Cities: Skylines
games.summary: A city builder in which road-following zones, agent citizens who route to work along computed paths, district policies, and player-drawn transit lines make traffic flow the central design problem.

games.core_loop: zone and draw roads -> citizens choose homes, jobs, and routes by cost, time, and comfort -> taxes and fees fund services -> milestones grant development points and map tiles -> unlock transport and services -> expand
games.design_notes: Route choice is a weighted cost over time, comfort, money, and behavior, so parking fees, transit fares, and lane choice shift where agents go, and the first game's cap of about 65,000 rendered citizens is replaced by a hardware limit. One in-game day and night stands for a month, so daily traffic rhythms and seasonal climate run on different scales. The launch drew criticism for performance and its economy simulation, console versions were delayed indefinitely in 2024, and development moved from Colossal Order to Iceflake Studios after a November 2025 announcement.

mechanics.note: Residential, commercial, industrial, and office zones along roads, with signature buildings unlocked at milestones.
Vehicles spread across lanes, parking fees enter route cost, and accident checks run per road segment.
Citizens compare driving, transit, and walking with a cost combining time, comfort, money, and personal preference.
Development points are spent in a tree to unlock transport options and services.
Milestones grant development points and map tiles, from 9 starting tiles up to 441.
Each map has a preset climate; winters bring snow.
Floods, forest fires, and tornadoes, mitigated by disaster response services.
Each day and night cycle equals one simulated month.
Signature buildings and services change land value in their zone.
Tax rates, fees, and ordinances fund the city.
Paradox Mods since 2024-03-25; mods can override game code.
Citizens compare driving, transit, and walking using a cost of time, comfort, money, and personal behavior, and parking fees enter the driving cost.

games.name: Cities: Skylines II
games.summary: The sequel to Cities: Skylines, with citizens choosing routes by time, comfort, and money, a tech tree of development points, preset climates with seasons, and maps of up to 441 tiles.

games.core_loop: explore with units -> found and grow cities -> allocate production and research -> unlock advances and wonders -> expand, trade, or fight rivals -> win by conquest or the space race
games.design_notes: Meier and Shelley combined the technology tree of Francis Tresham's board game with Empire's exploration and conquest and Railroad Tycoon's idea of several interacting systems managed at once; a SimCity-style zoning layer in an early prototype was dropped. Each city works surrounding terrain tiles for food, production, and trade, a worked-tile yield model the taxonomy does not yet name (proposal worked-tile-yields), and battles resolve from unit attack and defense values (proposal stat-combat-resolution). Wonders exist once per world, so building one denies it to every rival.

mechanics.note: Advances are researched one at a time through a prerequisite graph adapted from Tresham's 1980 board game, from Pottery and the Wheel to Nuclear Fission and Space Flight; each unlocks units, city improvements, wonders, or governments, so research order shapes the game.
Turns run from 4000 BC to as late as AD 2100; each turn every city produces and every unit moves, against two to seven AI civilizations.
The map starts hidden and is revealed by exploring units; barbarians emerge from huts, unclaimed land, and the sea, and become rarer as exploration proceeds.
Relations with rival civilizations lead to alliances, peace, or war.
Government forms unlocked by research change the economic and military rules of the civilization.
The player sets tax rates and the share of trade spent on research.
Cities track content and unhappy citizens; luxuries, temples, and wonders keep cities out of civil disorder.
Settlers build roads and later railroads that speed movement between cities.
Random worlds are generated for each game, with an alternative Earth map.
Corruption removes part of each city's trade, rising with distance from the Palace and depending on government type; a Courthouse reduces it.
Cities are captured by moving a military unit into them, transferring the city and its worked tiles to the conqueror.
Combat compares the attacker's attack value with the defender's defense under terrain and fortification modifiers and a random draw, and the loser is destroyed.

games.name: Sid Meier's Civilization
games.summary: A turn-based 4X game in which the player guides a civilization from 4000 BC toward the space age by founding cities, researching a technology tree, building one-per-world wonders, and competing with rival civilizations by diplomacy or war.

games.core_loop: read the scenario briefing -> set doctrine, emissions control, and weapon release authority -> assign units to patrol, strike, and support missions -> sensors detect and classify contacts -> weapons engage under doctrine -> adjust missions as detections and losses accrue
games.design_notes: CMO simulates the sensor and weapon chain rather than abstract unit strengths: detection depends on radar propagation, terrain, thermal layers, and weather, and engagement depends on database specifications and doctrine. The player works mostly at mission and doctrine level and lets tactical AI fly and fight, so one player can run scenarios from patrol-boat skirmishes to global war. The Command engine also has a Professional Edition with full database editing, umpire-controlled multiplayer, and Monte Carlo analysis, sold to defense organizations.

mechanics.note: Every platform's sensors and weapons come from a database of tens of thousands of real systems; radar propagation, sensor degradation, terrain masking, sonar thermal layers, weather, jamming, and anti-radiation strikes are modeled for thousands of active platforms in real time.
Each side sees only what its sensors detect; emission control (EMCON) policies trade a unit's own detection range against revealing it to enemy passive sensors.
Units are assigned to patrol, strike, and support missions and executed by tactical AI under doctrine settings such as weapon release authority and EMCON.
Contacts begin unidentified and are classified as sensor data accumulates.
Direct orders override a unit's mission behavior.
Scenarios lasting hours to days of game time run with time acceleration and pause.
Over 600 official and community scenarios plus a quick battle generator.
A Lua scripting engine and scenario editor let players build custom operations.
Scenarios are shared through the Steam Workshop.
Weather degrades sensors and affects engagements.
Ballistics are among the modeled effects alongside sensor propagation, so weapon flight and impact follow database specifications.

games.name: Command: Modern Operations
games.summary: A real-time operational military simulation in which the player commands air, naval, and land units drawn from a database of tens of thousands of real platforms, sensors, and weapons on a map of Earth, managing doctrine, emissions control, and missions.

games.core_loop: check documents -> search the vehicle with UV light and tools -> extract contraband or approve -> arrest or chase fleeing smugglers -> earn cash -> upgrade the post, cars, and defenses -> story missions and raids
games.design_notes: It moves the Papers, Please inspection loop into a 3D first-person space: document discrepancies are found on paper, but contraband is found physically by examining the vehicle with a UV flashlight and extracting it with tools. The number of documents per entrant grows over time, raising the error rate at constant attention. Inspection income funds post upgrades whose maintenance costs rise, while authored special assignments, chases, and gang raids interrupt the shift loop.

mechanics.note: Drivers present documents whose number grows over the campaign; small discrepancies require refusal, and suspicious vehicles are searched with a UV flashlight before tools extract hidden goods.
The player walks the post in first person, opens and searches vehicles, drives upgradable police cars in pursuits, and uses firearms in shootouts.
Cash from inspections, foiled smuggling, and interventions pays for upgrades while post maintenance costs rise over time.
Gang attacks on the post are countered with purchased defense upgrades.
Special assignments and story decisions shape the fate of Acaristan and lead to multiple endings.

games.name: Contraband Police
games.summary: A first-person border-post sim set in 1981 in which the player checks drivers' documents, searches vehicles for hidden contraband, chases smugglers, and upgrades the post against gang attacks.

claims.text: Norn genetics are haploid, with no dominant or recessive genes and no recombination between loci, and mutation can disable organs or produce Norns that cannot see or hear.

games.core_loop: hatch eggs -> Norns act on biochemical drives -> player rewards, punishes, and teaches words -> neural weights shift toward drive-reducing actions -> Norns breed and pass mutated genomes -> next generation behaves differently
games.design_notes: Steve Grand built each Norn as a stack of coupled models rather than a scripted pet: a neural network whose sight neurons are grouped one per object type, a biochemistry of chemicals and organs that sets drive levels, and a haploid genome with no dominance that codes for both. Learning is behaviorist: high drive levels act as punishment and reductions as reward, so the player's tickles and slaps only matter through the same chemistry. Because the genome builds the brain and body, mutations produce Norns that cannot see, lack organs, or never die, which the online breeding community catalogued and traded. Norns live about 40 hours, short enough for many generations.

mechanics.note: A neural-network brain maps sensed objects and drives to actions; drive reduction reinforces the action that preceded it, and the hand's tickle and slap act as reward and punishment through the same pathway.
Haploid digital genomes with no dominant or recessive genes encode brain wiring, biochemistry, and organs; offspring genomes mutate, and every boxed copy shipped a unique starting set of egg genomes.
Drives such as hunger and tiredness are concentrations in a simulated biochemistry that rise over time and fall when actions such as eating or resting succeed.
The player's hand pointer feeds Norns, shows them objects, and tickles or slaps them; neglect leads to hunger, disease, and death, but care shapes behavior only indirectly through learning.
Players teach nouns by naming objects a Norn is looking at and verbs with a learning computer, then type instructions that the Norn may choose to obey.
Norns hatch, grow, breed, and die within roughly 40 hours of play.
Grendels steal food, injure Norns, and carry diseases that sicken the population.
Exported Norns and genomes were swapped and bred across players by a large online community.

games.name: Creatures
games.summary: An artificial-life game in which the player hatches and raises Norns whose neural-network brains, simulated biochemistry, and haploid digital genomes produce learned behavior and heritable mutation.

games.core_loop: play the current ruler -> manage vassal opinion, council, and stress -> arrange marriages, schemes, and wars over claims -> ruler dies -> heir inherits titles under succession law -> realm fragments or consolidates
games.design_notes: CK3 makes the player a character rather than a state: realm strength depends on vassals whose itemized opinions, traits, and family ties decide whether they serve or rebel. Succession laws make death the main source of disruption, and stress penalizes playing a character against type, which pushes players to roleplay their traits. Event content is authored but fired from on_actions and character state, so the same templates produce different stories in different courts; culture and religion conversion is not yet a mechanic in the taxonomy (proposal culture-religion-conversion).

mechanics.note: On death, play passes to the player heir and titles pass under the realm's succession law, so partition can split a realm among children; the game ends if no viable heir remains, and dynasty heads spend Renown on bonuses for every dynasty member.
Personality, education, and genetic traits modify the six skills (Diplomacy, Martial, Stewardship, Intrigue, Learning, Prowess), opinions, and which event options a character can take.

Each character's opinion of another is an itemized list of modifiers from traits, relations, actions, and events, many expiring over time; discontented vassals join factions pressing for independence, a rival claimant, or less crown authority.
Skills grow from education and from perks in six lifestyles, each with three skill trees.
Friends, rivals, and lovers form between characters and shift opinions and event outcomes.
Marriages create alliances and heirs, making match choice a political decision.
Genetic traits such as strong or poor health pass to children.
Vassal factions accumulate strength and can revolt when their demands are refused.
Wars are fought over claims, and marriages and alliances link realms.
Events are called from on_actions, decisions, and interactions, with weighted options and scheduled follow-ups.
Lifestyle perk trees and cultural innovations unlock abilities and buildings.
Nested tooltips let players open explanations of terms inside other tooltips.

Acting against personality traits and suffering events add stress; crossing stress levels fires mental-break events whose coping options can add traits (from level 2 up), and extreme stress can kill the character.
Prestige and piety accrue from rank, traits, and deeds and are spent on actions such as creating titles (prestige) and faith decisions (piety).
Counties carry a faith and a culture; the court chaplain can convert a county's faith and the steward can promote the ruler's culture, while faith hostility sets opinion penalties from 0 to -30.
Counties belong to titles with de jure hierarchies, and wars are fought to press claims on them; conquered counties start with low county control.
War score from battles and occupation lets the attacker enforce the war goal at full score, while either side can offer white peace.
Battles resolve from army size, men-at-arms, knights, commander skill, and terrain, in phases that run until one side is routed.

games.name: Crusader Kings III
games.summary: A character-driven grand strategy game in which the player rules as successive heads of a medieval dynasty from 867 or later to 1453, managing traits, stress, vassal opinion, marriages, and succession across a map of feudal titles.

claims.text: The `year` value records the 2008 release of DCS: Black Shark, the first DCS title (Russia 17 October, English 10 December 2008); the free DCS World platform entered open beta in May 2012.

games.core_loop: pick a module and mission -> cold start through cockpit switches -> fly and navigate -> find targets with sensors -> employ weapons and survive defenses -> recover and land -> debrief
games.design_notes: DCS treats each aircraft as a set of subsystems (engines, fuel, electrical, hydraulics, radios, sensors) operated through individually clickable cockpit controls, so procedures and failures follow from system state rather than scripts. Its fidelity reaches professional use: the U.S. Air Force's 355th Training Squadron has used the A-10C module, and French and Ukrainian pilots have trained on modules. The business model is a free base with two aircraft and two maps, with paid aircraft and map modules from Eagle Dynamics and third parties sharing one client.

mechanics.note: Aircraft modules are built from real-world data; the F-16C uses a professional flight model with a fly-by-wire flight control system.
Clickable cockpits operate modeled engines, fuel, electrical, hydraulic, and radio systems, so start-up and weapon employment follow real procedures.
Missions pit aircraft against air and ground units with sensors and weapons; users host PvE and PvP servers running their own missions.
The mission editor builds single-player and multiplayer missions with Lua scripting.
Lua mission scripting and third-party module development extend the platform.
Missiles, bombs, and gun rounds fly as simulated projectiles, so release parameters such as speed, altitude, and range decide hits.
Damage affects individual modeled subsystems such as engines, hydraulics, and electrical systems, changing how the aircraft flies and what still works.

games.name: DCS World
games.summary: A combat flight sim platform of study-level aircraft modules with clickable cockpits and modeled subsystems, flown in missions and on multiplayer servers built with a Lua-scriptable mission editor.

games.core_loop: spend political capital to adjust policy sliders -> effects propagate through the weighted policy network -> statistics, situations, and voter group happiness shift -> resolve dilemmas and events -> make election promises -> win or lose the election
games.design_notes: Democracy 4 models a country as one visible causal graph: policies, statistics, situations, and voter groups are nodes, and the interface shows the weighted links in and out of each. The player is constrained by political capital, earned through loyal ministers and spent on policy changes, and by voters who belong to several groups at once. Political capital as a regenerating action currency is not yet a mechanic in the taxonomy (proposal political-capital).

mechanics.note: Policies in seven areas (tax, economy, welfare, foreign policy, transport, law and order, public services) are sliders; the engine treats voters, groups, policies, ministers, and events as neurons in a homebrew network with bounded values, so weighted effects move statistics such as crime and air quality and the happiness of voter groups.
Before each general election the player makes two promises to the electorate; broken promises raise voter cynicism, and losing the election ends the game.

Voter groups such as the religious, patriotic, parents, capitalists, socialists, liberals, and conservatives overlap, since each voter belongs to several, so pleasing every group is nearly impossible.
Dilemmas, such as appointing a senior judge, must be resolved before the turn can end.
Introducing or cancelling a policy costs political capital.
Excessive taxes cause tax evasion.
Deficits add to national debt that the player must pay down.
Situations such as pollution or homelessness persist while conditions hold, and events arrive outside player control.
Political capital, earned through loyal ministers, is spent each turn to introduce, cancel, or adjust policies, so it caps how fast the government can change.

games.name: Democracy 4
games.summary: A turn-based government sim in which the player, as leader of a democracy, adjusts policy sliders whose weighted effects move statistics and overlapping voter groups, resolves dilemmas, and tries to balance the budget and win the next election.

games.core_loop: explore a generated world by day -> gather and craft tools, food, and light -> manage hunger, health, and sanity -> survive nights, hounds, and seasons -> build a base and stockpile for winter -> die and start a new world
games.design_notes: Three meters interact: empty hunger drains health, and sanity falls at dusk and night and from unpleasant actions until, below 15% of maximum, shadow creatures attack, so the mind is a survival stock alongside the body. The 8-minute day is divided into day, dusk, and night segments whose split shifts with the season, and total darkness is lethal because Charlie attacks anyone without a light. Hound attacks escalate on a schedule tied to days survived, and death deletes the world except through rare resurrection items. Klei released it in beta in 2012 and fully on 23 April 2013.

mechanics.note: Hunger, health, and sanity meters; default maximum hunger is 150 and drains 75 per game day, and at empty hunger health drains 1.25 per second until the player eats or dies.
Recipes combine gathered items into tools, light, shelter, and weapons; most must first be prototyped at a crafting station such as the science machine, though some characters bypass this.

A day lasts 8 real minutes in sixteen 30-second segments of day, dusk, and night; sanity drains 5 per minute at dusk and 50 per minute in total darkness, where Charlie attacks unless the player has light.
Winter shortens days and lengthens nights; seasons change hazards.
Hound attacks scale with days survived, from 2 hounds every 5-8 days early to 7-10 hounds every 11-16 days after day 100, with shorter warnings.
Food spoils over time; spoiled food restores less hunger and costs health and sanity.
Picked grass, saplings, and berry bushes regrow.
Fire spreads across flammable plants and structures.
Each world is randomly generated.
Death deletes the world unless a rare resurrection item is available.

games.name: Don't Starve
games.summary: A survival sim in a procedurally generated wilderness where the player balances hunger, health, and sanity, crafts tools and light, and prepares for darkness, hounds, and seasons.

aliases: Slaves to Armok: God of Blood Chapter II: Dwarf Fortress
games.core_loop: embark and dig -> designate jobs, stockpiles, and workshops -> dwarves self-assign labors and craft -> needs, emotions, and stress accumulate -> migrants, caravans, sieges, and beasts arrive -> fortress thrives or collapses into the world's legends
games.design_notes: Tarn Adams's stated principles are to break a system into parts, avoid overplanning, and base each model on a real-world analog; he describes the game as a story generator. The fortress is embarked inside a world whose geology and history were already simulated, and the fortress's own events flow back into that history through Legends, so a collapse becomes a record that a later adventurer can visit. Strange moods let an inspired dwarf seize a workshop to make a named artifact and go insane if materials are missing, which turns the production system into a story source. The game was free and donation-funded from 2006; a paid Steam edition with sprite graphics followed in December 2022, still short of a 1.0 version.

mechanics.note: World generation builds elevation, rainfall, drainage, temperature, and vegetation layers, then simulates civilizations, sites, and historical figures for a player-chosen number of years before the fortress is embarked.
The player designates digging, chopping, construction, and workshop jobs; dwarves with the matching labor enabled pick them up, and a manager can queue work orders automatically.

Emotions add to or subtract from a hidden stress value (-1,000,000 to +1,000,000) with effects from +10,000, +25,000, and +50,000; stressed dwarves throw tantrums, fall into depression, or wander obliviously, prolonged stress leads to insanity, and one breakdown can spread unhappiness.

Body parts are layered tissues (skin, fat, muscle, bone, nerves) damaged individually in combat; injuries can be permanent and are treated in a hospital with traction benches, casts, sutures, and splints.
Water and magma flow tile by tile with up to seven depth levels per tile, so breaching a river, cavern lake, or magma source floods connected tunnels.
Z-levels, added in 2007, let the fortress descend level by level through soil and stone to caverns, the magma sea, and the underworld, connected by stairs and ramps.
Legends mode lists historical figures, sites, artifacts, and civilizations with a historical map; fortress deeds and retired adventurers are added, and the archive exports to XML.
Work quality and speed rise with skill gained through practice in each labor.
Food, drink, and sleep, plus personal needs such as socializing or praying met at taverns, temples, and libraries.
Emotions become short-term memories; strong or revisited ones are promoted to long-term memories that keep adding stress.
Facets such as bravery, stress vulnerability, and anxiety scale how stress builds and dissipates.
Friends, family, and pets; their deaths are major stressors.
Ore is smelted to bars and alloyed; steel needs flux to make pig iron plus coke or charcoal, and magma can replace fuel.
Tiles, materials, and creatures carry temperatures.
Fires spread and burn dwarves and furniture.
Ambushes, sieges, megabeasts, and forgotten beasts are met with squads, fortifications, and traps triggered by levers or pressure plates.
Wealthier and more populous fortresses attract sieges and megabeasts.
Migrant waves from the mountainhome grow as the fortress develops.
Yearly caravans from neighboring civilizations are handled by a broker; caravans can be absent or hostile depending on history.
Furniture defines bedrooms, dining halls, and offices; nobles demand rooms of rising value.
A justice system punishes assault, murder, and vandalism.
Underground farming on soil layers; plump helmet mushrooms are brewed into wine.
Dwarves carry goods to player-defined stockpiles.
Military squads in uniforms train at barracks and can be ordered to attack.

Emotions from events add to or subtract from a hidden stress value (-1,000,000 to +1,000,000) scaled by facets such as stress vulnerability and bravery; above +10,000, +25,000, and +50,000 dwarves risk tantrums, depression, obliviousness, and insanity, and long-term memories keep adding stress.

games.name: Dwarf Fortress
games.summary: A colony sim in which the player directs a fortress of autonomous dwarves inside a procedurally generated world whose history, geology, fluids, bodies, and minds are all simulated.

claims.text: Dyson Sphere Program was still labeled Early Access on Steam when accessed in October 2026, so no full-release year is recorded.
Reviewers compare it favorably to Factorio and Satisfactory, but the cited source names only Stellaris as a design inspiration, so no Factorio influence edge is recorded.

games.core_loop: mine planetary veins -> belt ores through smelters and assemblers -> craft matrix cubes for research -> link planets and stars with logistics stations -> launch solar sails and carrier rockets -> Dyson sphere power feeds endgame production
games.design_notes: Dyson Sphere Program scales the factory puzzle from one map to a randomly generated cluster of stars: each planet is a rotating sphere whose day-night cycle affects solar power, and logistics stations match per-item local and remote supply and demand, sending up to 100 drones within a planet and 10 vessels between planets or, with Space Warpers, between stars. The Dyson sphere is a megastructure designed in a node-and-frame editor and built by ejecting solar sails (36 kW each at base, scaled by star luminosity, expiring after 5,400 seconds unless captured by a completed shell) and launching carrier rockets; ray receivers return its energy to planets or convert it to critical photons. The December 2023 Dark Fog update added hives and planetary bases whose threat rises with the player's power generation and combat, a variant of pollution-driven aggression. The developers drew inspiration from Stellaris, which included Dyson sphere construction. The sphere works as a goal sink that absorbs very large quantities of sails and rockets; no taxonomy mechanic covers such megaproject sinks, so this run proposed one.

mechanics.note: Smelters, assemblers, chemical plants, refineries, and particle colliders run fixed recipes that build up to six matrix cube types and Dyson sphere components; proliferator coating adds extra products or speed.
Three belt tiers carry items between sorters and machines on a planetary grid that wraps around a sphere and narrows toward the poles.
Labs in research mode consume matrix cubes in technology-specific mixes, all stacked labs working on the front of one queue; labs can instead be switched to manufacture matrices.
Mining machines and advanced miners extract iron, copper, titanium, silicon, and rare veins whose distribution differs by planet and star type; pumps and oil extractors tap fluids.

Wind, thermal, solar, fusion, and artificial-star generators feed tower-linked grids; logistics stations charge at 30 to 300 MW, and Dyson sphere energy reaches planets through ray receivers at 30% base efficiency.
The Dyson sphere editor places nodes, frames, and shells on multiple orbital layers around a star, and its power output depends on built structure and absorbed sails.
Dark Fog planetary bases and space hives attack factories and the player's mech, countered by turrets, energy shields, and player combat units.
Dark Fog threat accumulates from the player's power generation and from combat, bases and hives gain levels from experience, and aggressiveness settings scale attack sizes.
Each seed generates a star cluster with star types, planet types, and mineral distributions, including neutron stars, white dwarfs, and black holes.
Layouts are saved and pasted as blueprints, and the mech's construction drones place them.
Planets rotate around their axes and orbit their stars, so solar panel output varies with the local day.
Storage boxes, tanks, and per-slot capacity in logistics stations buffer flows between planets.
The Icarus mech hand-crafts early buildings from inventory before assemblers take over.
The player flies the Icarus mech across planets and through space to build within its range.

The Dyson sphere is designed in a node-and-frame editor and built from solar sails fired by EM-Rail Ejectors and frames carried by rockets; unabsorbed sails expire after 5,400 seconds, and the finished sphere's energy feeds endgame production.
Proliferator coating on input items lets the consuming machine choose extra products or faster production.

Logistics stations set each item slot to local or remote supply, demand, or storage and are paired automatically by priority; up to 100 drones per station haul within a planet and 10 vessels between planets, with range and minimum-load sliders.

games.name: Dyson Sphere Program
games.summary: A 3D factory automation game in which the player's mech builds production lines on rotating planets, links star systems with logistics drones and warp vessels, and launches sails and rockets to assemble Dyson spheres around stars.

games.core_loop: gather from the shared ecosystem -> specialize in skills and craft at tables -> trade through player stores and currencies -> propose and vote on laws and taxes -> research technology to stop the meteor -> manage pollution and species populations before impact
games.design_notes: Eco makes the ecosystem a shared commons: each player's harvesting and pollution changes species populations and the climate for everyone on the server. Its answer to overexploitation is player-made institutions rather than designer rules, with enforceable laws, taxes, and currencies, and simulation data that players can cite as evidence in debates. It began as an educational project funded in part by the U.S. Department of Education.

mechanics.note: Thousands of plants and animals from dozens of species grow across the world; overhunting or overharvesting can drive a species extinct, and a disruption in one species cascades across the planet.
Mining waste and industrial pollution poison rivers and kill farms, and excessive air pollution raises sea levels.

Players propose laws in a programmable rule system and vote on them, the game enforces ratified laws, and elections set tax rates and community funds; governments range from dictatorships to lawless, trust-based communities.
A meteor is set to strike in thirty days, and players must gather resources and research technology to stop it without harming the world.
Plant and animal populations recover over time unless harvested faster than they regrow; cutting too many trees reduces how much air pollution is absorbed.
Accumulated pollution changes the climate and sea level.
Players run stores and currency exchanges with fiat or resource-backed currencies and set exchange rates.
Players post labor contracts for others to fulfill.
Varied food and larger homes earn skill points spent on specialties such as farming, hunting, trade, and engineering.
More than 30 craft tables turn materials into goods across hundreds of recipes.
Each world is bounded by a meteor due in thirty days, so a server's run ends with stopping it or with impact, and servers are commonly wiped and restarted as fresh worlds.

games.name: Eco
games.summary: A multiplayer civilization survival game in which players on one server share a simulated ecosystem, specialize in skills, craft and trade with player-made currencies, and pass enforceable laws while researching how to stop a meteor due in thirty days without wrecking the environment.

games.core_loop: buy cargo at a station -> hyperspace to a system within fuel range -> fight or evade pirates and police -> dock by matching the station's rotation -> sell for profit -> buy weapons and equipment -> raise combat rating
games.design_notes: Each of the eight galaxies and its 256 systems is regenerated from a seed rather than stored, which let a large universe fit in an 8-bit micro and made procedural generation the core of the design. Commodity prices differ by system, and fuel limits each hyperjump to 7 light years, so route choice is the main economic decision. The goal of reaching the Elite combat rank is open-ended; the player chooses between trading, piracy, bounty hunting, and mining.

mechanics.note: Eight galaxies of 256 planets each are generated from seed numbers at runtime; each system's name, economy, government, and description derive from the seed.
Commodity prices vary by system economy; the player buys cheap and sells dear between systems, constrained by cargo bay size and the 7 light-year fuel limit per jump.
Real-time wireframe dogfights and manual docking that requires matching a rotating station's spin unless a docking computer is bought.
Legal status (clean, offender, fugitive) worsens with piracy and illegal cargo and draws police ships.
Combat rating rises with kills from Harmless toward Elite; most versions also offer Galactic Navy missions with special rewards.
Mining lasers break asteroids into fragments that can be scooped and sold.

games.name: Elite
games.summary: A 3D space trading and combat game in which the player flies a single ship through eight seed-generated galaxies, buying and selling cargo and fighting pirates and police to raise a combat rating.

games.core_loop: take missions or cargo at a station -> jump between star systems -> trade, fight, mine, or explore -> earn credits, rank, and faction influence -> outfit or buy ships -> background simulation shifts faction control and system states
games.design_notes: Stellar Forge generates around 400 billion star systems from rules of star and planet formation and blends in about 150,000 systems from real astronomical data, so the galaxy is mostly unvisited. The server-side Background Simulation tracks minor-faction influence, economy, and states per system and updates them from what all players do, so Solo, Private Group, and Open players share one political map. Ship capability comes from outfitting modules within power and mass limits, and flight is Newtonian with a default flight-assist layer.

mechanics.note: One galaxy state is shared by Open, Private Group, and Solo players; Frontier's Background Simulation changes faction influence, system states, and markets over time from aggregate player activity.
Stellar Forge generates a 1:1 Milky Way of about 400 billion systems, bodies, and landable planetary surfaces, blended with about 150,000 catalog systems.
Six-axis Newtonian flight with optional flight assist; manual docking, supercruise approaches, and combat that balances power distributor pips and heat.
Station markets differ by economy type; traders haul commodities between stations for price differences, limited by cargo capacity and jump range.
Market supply and demand at each station shift prices as players buy and sell.
Minor factions hold influence shares per system and enter wars or elections when two factions' influence is close; Powerplay pledges players to one of 12 powers contesting territory.
Standing with minor factions and superpower navy ranks gate missions and system permits.
Mission boards offer delivery, combat, and data missions with deadlines and payouts that also move faction influence.
Ships take modules in fixed slots (power plant, thrusters, frame shift drive, hardpoints); module mass and class set jump range, speed, and loadout.
A power plant's output must cover module draw; over budget, modules shut down by player-set priority.
Ship heat rises from weapons, fuel scooping near stars, and damage; overheating damages modules, and heat sinks dump it.
Mining lasers, collector limpets, and sub-surface charges extract ore from planetary rings.
Squadrons and player-supported minor factions coordinate background simulation work.
System bodies are unknown until scanned; first discoverers are credited.

The power distributor's pips are split among systems, engines, and weapons capacitors in flight, setting each capacitor's recharge; module priorities decide what shuts down when the power plant is over budget.
Each ship module has its own integrity, and damage to the power plant, thrusters, or drive degrades or disables it until repaired.
About 150,000 star systems from real astronomical catalogs are blended into the procedurally generated galaxy.

games.name: Elite Dangerous
games.summary: An online space sim set in a 1:1 procedurally generated Milky Way where players trade, fight, mine, and explore while a server-side background simulation shifts faction control from aggregate player actions.

games.core_loop: plant grasses to spread biomes -> place plants and animals whose requirements are met -> healthy species live longer, breed, and earn diversity points -> spend points on new species, genetic modifications, and evolutions -> complete tasks for rewards
games.design_notes: Equilinox, built solo by ThinMatrix, ties its economy to ecological fit: each species has a life cycle and requirements, and healthy individuals live longer, breed more, and yield more diversity points, the currency for new species and modifications. Evolution is a gated unlock (meet a species' evolution conditions, then pay to evolve) rather than simulated selection, which keeps the 120+ species on an authored progression. Biomes spread from planted grasses, so terrain type is itself a player-placed stock. Paid genetic modification matches the genome-modification proposal from run catalog-ge.

mechanics.note: Each species needs a biome, food, and nearby plants or water; satisfied individuals stay healthy, live longer, and breed, while unmet needs reduce health.
Species evolve into new species once their conditions are met and points are paid, and 60+ tasks grant points or content.
Diversity points earned by healthy plants and animals are the single currency for buying species, modifications, and evolutions; repeatable tasks let players farm a steady income.
Plants and animals grow, eat, reproduce, and die on species-specific cycles.
Some animals hunt others, so predator placement constrains prey populations.
Planted grasses convert ground into one of 10 biome types, and algae turns water into river for fish.

games.name: Equilinox
games.summary: A relaxed nature-building game in which the player spreads biomes with grasses, places plants and animals that each have environmental requirements, and spends diversity points earned by healthy species on evolutions and genetic modifications.

games.core_loop: take a cargo job -> couple the trailer -> drive the route paying fuel and tolls -> deliver on time with little damage -> earn money and experience -> spend skill points and buy trucks, garages, and drivers -> longer and riskier jobs
games.design_notes: The pleasure is long-haul driving through a compressed map (71 cities in 12 countries in the base game), with economic pressure from delivery deadlines, fuel, tolls, and repair costs and with damage deducted from pay. Progression is a skill-point tree that unlocks cargo classes (ADR hazardous, long distance, valuable, fragile, urgent, eco driving), plus a company layer in which owned garages host hired AI drivers who earn money off-screen. Multiplayer began as the fan mod TruckersMP in 2013 before official support in 2021.

mechanics.note: Licensed trucks with modeled engines and gearboxes pull trailers whose cargo changes acceleration and braking; collisions damage truck, trailer, and cargo.
Jobs specify cargo, destination, and a time limit; less damage earns more money and experience, while fuel, tolls, and repairs are paid from earnings.
A continuous road map linking European cities sets route distance, tolls, and travel time.
Skill points from experience unlock ADR, long-distance, valuable, fragile, urgent, and eco-driving jobs.
Recruitment agencies supply AI drivers who work from owned garages and return income.
A bank loan is the alternative to saving 100,000 euros for the first truck.
Damage requires paid maintenance at service shops.

games.name: Euro Truck Simulator 2
games.summary: A truck driving sim in which the player hauls timed cargo deliveries across a scaled European road network and grows a transport company of trucks, garages, and hired drivers.

games.core_loop: accrue administrative, diplomatic, and military monarch points -> buy technology, stability, ideas, and development -> steer trade and colonize -> ally and declare wars -> occupy and annex provinces -> manage unrest, estates, and coalitions
games.design_notes: EU4 converts ruler quality into three spendable currencies (administrative, diplomatic, and military monarch points) that buy technology, stability, ideas, and province development, which makes each succession an economic event. Expansion is checked by systems rather than scripts: aggressive expansion feeds defensive coalitions, and conquered provinces stay restless until integrated. Monarch points, war score, province integration, and missionary conversion are not yet mechanics in the taxonomy (proposals political-capital, war-score-peace, territorial-claims-integration, culture-religion-conversion).

mechanics.note: Alliances, vassals, tributaries, and royal marriages bind nations; aggressive expansion raises other nations' hostility until they form a defensive coalition against the expander.

Trade value generated in provinces flows downstream through a fixed directed network of trade nodes; merchants either collect in a node or steer value toward the player's home node, and trade power in each node sets the share taken.
Provinces accumulate unrest from foreign culture, religion, and recent conquest, and high unrest spawns rebel armies; national stability is a separate stock raised with administrative monarch points.
Administrative, diplomatic, and military technology tracks are bought with matching monarch points; institutions such as feudalism spread between provinces and raise technology cost until embraced.
Estates hold loyalty and influence over the crown and grant bonuses or demands.
Each monarch's administrative, diplomatic, and military skill sets monthly monarch point income; on death an heir succeeds, with risks of regency, succession wars, or personal unions.
AI opinion of the player is an itemized sum of modifiers such as improved relations, royal marriage, and aggressive expansion.
Historical and flavor events fire from national history and current state.
Prestige and power projection modify diplomacy and stability.
Idea groups, policies, and government reforms change national rules.
Deficits are covered by loans, and unmanageable debt ends in bankruptcy.

Administrative, diplomatic, and military monarch points accrue monthly from the ruler's skills (plus advisors) and buy technology, ideas, stability, and province development, so each succession changes the nation's budget of action.

A national corruption value accumulates from several state conditions and falls with a monthly budget line for rooting out corruption; while high it raises the cost of technology and other state actions.
Provinces have a culture and a religion; missionaries convert province religion over time against resistance, and non-state religion or non-accepted culture adds unrest.

Provinces have an owner and a controller; sieges flip control, peace deals transfer ownership, and new provinces must be cored with administrative power, with uncored land adding overextension and unrest.
War score from battles, occupation, and the war goal caps peace demands, each priced in score (provinces, gold, vassalage).
Land battles roll dice each phase of fire and shock, modified by general skill and terrain, and drain each army's strength and morale until one side retreats.

games.name: Europa Universalis IV
games.summary: A real-time-with-pause grand strategy game in which the player directs one of over 500 nations from 1444 to 1821 through monarch-point spending, trade-node competition, colonization, diplomacy, and war on a province map.

games.core_loop: train skills in real time -> mine, salvage, or run missions for materials and ISK -> manufacture or buy ships and modules on the player market -> fit ships and fly into space of a chosen security level -> lose ships in combat and replace them -> corporations and alliances fight over sovereignty
games.design_notes: EVE keeps one economy for all players: nearly everything is player-made and ship losses are permanent, so wars create manufacturing demand. Risk and reward are tied to space security, with the most profitable activities in low-sec and null-sec, where the NPC police do not destroy aggressors. CCP hired an economist in 2007 to oversee the economy. Security-graded zones and permanent asset loss on destruction are not yet mechanics in the taxonomy (proposals pvp-security-zones, loss-on-death).

mechanics.note: Players gather raw materials and manufacture nearly all ships and modules, then trade them in a supply-and-demand market with price history charts, where manipulation such as ramping and bear raids is possible.

One shared universe on the Tranquility server holds more than 5,000 stargate-linked systems plus about 2,500 wormhole systems; system security from 1.0 to -1.0 sets whether CONCORD police destroy aggressors.
Corporations led by a CEO assign roles, tax members, declare wars for a weekly fee, and join alliances that claim sovereignty over null-sec systems.
Skills have prerequisites, and capital-ship skills take several times longer to train than frigate skills.
Skills train in real time, including while logged off, from a queue of up to 50 skills.
Ships are fitted with modules in high, mid, and low slots plus semi-permanent rigs.
Blueprints turn gathered materials into ships and modules.
Players mine asteroids and salvage wrecks for materials.
Players elect the Council of Stellar Management, which carries requests to CCP; the first election in 2008 had 66 candidates for nine seats.
Unprovoked aggression in secure space costs security status and draws police response.
A destroyed ship and its fittings are gone for good, part of its cargo and modules drops in a lootable wreck, and ship insurance pays back part of the hull's value.

Each system's security from 1.0 to -1.0 decides whether CONCORD police destroy aggressors; high-sec deters player attacks, low- and null-sec leave them to players, and the riskier zones hold the richer activities.

games.name: EVE Online
games.summary: A single-universe space MMO in which players mine, manufacture, trade, and fight in ships that are destroyed for good, inside a player-made economy and a galaxy of high-, low-, and null-security space where player alliances claim sovereignty.

games.core_loop: type to or touch Grace and Trip -> parser maps input to a discourse act -> characters react and tension shifts -> drama manager picks the next beat -> secrets surface -> the couple reconciles, splits, or throws the player out
games.design_notes: Michael Mateas and Andrew Stern built Façade as a research artifact: Grace and Trip are written in A Behavior Language (ABL) as reactive behaviors, and a drama manager picks the next story beat from an authored library to follow a tension arc toward a climax. Typed text is mapped to a small set of discourse acts (the Versu paper counts 30 parameterized speech acts and 27 beats), which lets a limited body of authored dialogue answer open-ended input. It is a boundary case: the simulated systems are the parser, character behaviors, and beat sequencing over mostly authored dialogue, built for replay so players can find other outcomes.

mechanics.note: Typed sentences are matched by keywords and context to discourse acts such as agreeing, criticizing, or flirting, which Grace and Trip answer in character.
A drama manager chooses the next beat whose preconditions match the state, steering toward a rising tension arc and one of three endings.
Revelations such as a confessed affair fire only when earlier beats and player choices set them up.
As the couple argues, the player's responses read as taking one side, which shapes later beats.
The player walks around the apartment in first person and can click objects or body parts to hug, comfort, or kiss.

games.name: Façade
games.summary: A free 2005 interactive drama in which the player types natural language as a dinner guest of the married couple Grace and Trip while a drama manager sequences authored beats toward one of three endings.

claims.text: Factorio was publicly purchasable as an alpha from its official site in 2013, after the February 2013 Indiegogo campaign, three years before Steam early access on 2016-02-25; `year` records the 2013 alpha.
The design grew out of the Minecraft tech mods IndustrialCraft and BuildCraft, which lead designer Michal Kovarik cited; the `influenced_by` edge to Minecraft records that mod lineage.

games.core_loop: mine ore -> smelt and assemble on belts and inserters -> feed science packs to labs -> research new machines -> pollution draws biter attacks -> defend and expand outposts by rail -> launch a rocket
games.design_notes: Lead designer Michal Kovarik cited the Minecraft tech mods IndustrialCraft and BuildCraft; Factorio turned their pipes and machines into a standalone game where ratio planning and layout are the challenge. Item movement is discrete and deterministic (belts carry 15, 30, 45, or 60 items per second across two lanes), which makes throughput legible and lets the lockstep multiplayer simulate identical worlds. Pollution couples industry to combat: chunks above 15 units diffuse 2% to neighbors, spawners that absorb it send attack groups, and total pollution produced drives the enemy evolution factor. Each layer of logistics (belts, trains with block signals, roboport-based logistic and construction robots, circuit combinators) is a mechanic the player adopts when the previous one stops scaling, and blueprints let solved layouts be reused. Speed, productivity, and efficiency modules and beacons that trade power for throughput, and the rocket silo as a terminal sink for produced parts, have no taxonomy entry; this run proposed both.

mechanics.note: Assembling machines, furnaces, chemical plants, and refineries run fixed recipes with crafting times; science packs require multi-step trees from ore to circuits, oil products, and rocket parts.
Two-lane belts in four tiers carry 15, 30, 45, or 60 items per second; splitters, undergrounds, and lane priorities shape flow, and inserters move items between belts and machines.
Labs consume science packs of rising recipe complexity to research a technology graph that leads through oil processing, robots, and nuclear power to the rocket silo.
Electric and burner mining drills extract iron, copper, coal, stone, and uranium from ore patches at rates set by drill tier and mining productivity research; pumpjacks extract crude oil.
Machines emit pollution into 32x32 chunks; above 15 units a chunk diffuses 2% to each cardinal neighbor every 64 ticks, and water, grass, and trees absorb it.

Biter and spitter nests send attack groups when their chunk absorbs pollution, recruiting units at pollution costs from 4 for a small biter to 400 for a behemoth; turrets, walls, and flamethrowers defend.
An evolution factor rises with elapsed time, total pollution produced, and spawners destroyed, squashed as total over one plus total, and unlocks medium, big, and behemoth enemies.
Steam engines, solar panels, accumulators, and nuclear reactors feed a pole-connected grid; under shortage power is shared evenly so all machines slow proportionally.
Selected areas save to blueprints, books, and a personal library that persists across saves; exchange strings are shared online, and construction robots build pasted ghosts.
Rail and chain signals divide track into blocks that one train reserves at a time, letting train networks share track.
Trains run schedules of stations with wait conditions on cargo, time, inactivity, or circuit signals.
Red and green wires carry item-count signals into arithmetic, decider, constant, and (in 2.0) selector combinators that control inserters, belts, train stops, and lamps.
Pipes and pumps carry water, crude oil, petroleum, and steam; version 2.0 merged pipes into segments that share contents.
Ore tiles run out as they are mined, and crude oil wells decline toward a 20% yield floor, pushing expansion to new patches.
Chests, storage tanks, and the logistic network's storage chests buffer items, and full outputs stall machines upstream.
The engineer crafts early buildings and items from inventory using the same recipes as assemblers, with a crafting queue.
The Space Age expansion adds five quality levels from normal to legendary, raised by chance from quality modules, with a recycler that returns 25% of ingredients.
In Space Age, Gleba's agricultural products spoil over fixed timers into spoilage, and recipe outputs inherit ingredient freshness.
Mods use a modified Lua 5.2 with data and control stages and are distributed through an in-game mod portal; overhauls such as Krastorio 2 replace progression.
Production and consumption graphs per item over time windows and an electric network panel show where ratios fail.
Maps are generated from a seed with settings for ore frequency, size, and richness, water, cliffs, and enemy bases.
Space Age elevated rails let a second track layer cross over ground tracks and buildings.
The engineer walks the map, mines by hand early, and places buildings within reach, later driving cars, tanks, and spidertrons.
The rocket silo consumes rocket parts for each launch, and launching a rocket ends the base game; Space Age moves the goal to a space platform reaching the edge of the solar system.

Speed, productivity, efficiency, and (Space Age) quality modules fill machine slots, and beacons project module effects onto neighboring machines at a power cost; productivity bonuses are capped at +300%.

Roboports define logistic zones where logistic robots carry items among active provider, passive provider, storage, buffer, and requester chests by priority, one item per trip at 3 tiles per second before research.
Straight and curved rail pieces are placed to build train networks, with elevated rails in Space Age, and the rail planner lays segments between points.

games.name: Factorio
games.summary: A factory automation game in which the player builds belt, train, robot, and circuit networks that mine, refine, and assemble items on an alien planet while pollution provokes native biters that evolve over time.

games.core_loop: buy fields and machinery -> plow, seed, fertilize, and harvest with implements -> store or sell crops or feed productions and animals -> take contracts for extra income -> reinvest in land, buildings, and equipment
games.design_notes: Farming Simulator models agriculture as ordered field operations performed with specific implements, so the challenge is machine operation and fleet logistics rather than market strategy. FS25 lists 25 crop types including two rice varieties grown in paddies, spinach, peas, and green beans, adds water buffalo and goats, adds twisters and hail that damage crops, and deforms soft ground under tires. Dynamically generated contracts pay for work on other farms, and the in-game ModHub distributes developer-tested community vehicles, maps, and scripts.

mechanics.note: Fields move through cultivating or plowing, seeding, fertilizing, weeding, and harvesting with matching implements; 25 crop types follow seasonal calendars, with rice grown in paddies.
The player drives over 400 licensed vehicles and implements from more than 150 brands, each with its own power, speed, and weight; GPS-assisted steering automates straight passes.
Vehicles accumulate wear and damage that reduce performance until repaired at a workshop.
Tires leave tracks that deform soft ground.
Cows, sheep, pigs, chickens, horses, water buffalo, and goats with offspring need feed and care and yield products.
Productions and farm shops convert crops into processed goods as business ventures.
Dynamically generated contracts such as mowing, fertilizing, or hauling pay for work on other farmers' fields.
Hired AI helpers drive vehicles to work fields while the player does other tasks.
A seasonal cycle, introduced in FS22, sets planting and harvest windows.
Twisters and hail can damage crops.
Bank loans fund early expansion.
ModHub distributes developer-tested community mods that add vehicles, maps, and scripts.

games.name: Farming Simulator 25
games.summary: The 2024 entry in Giants Software's series in which the player runs a farm business by operating over 400 licensed vehicles and implements across seasonal field work, livestock, forestry, and production chains.

games.core_loop: gather, hunt, forage, and farm -> rotate crops to hold soil fertility -> feed a varied diet and supply clean water, clothing, and healers against disease -> upgrade housing and the town center as desirability rises -> fortify against raiders drawn by prosperity
games.design_notes: Farthest Frontier makes public health the main failure path: dysentery, cholera, tetanus, rabies, frostbite, and bubonic plague each have causes the player can address with clean water, clothing and shoes, healers, and rat catchers. Farming adds soil state, with 12 crops that must be rotated and fields improved by clearing weeds and rocks, and 19 food types with berries and greens preventing scurvy. Prosperity raises raider strength, so growth itself increases military pressure.

mechanics.note: Twelve crops with rotation to preserve soil fertility; fields improve by clearing weeds and rocks and adjusting the soil mix.
Dysentery, cholera, tetanus, rabies, frostbite, and plague spread or strike based on water, clothing, rats, and healer coverage.
Nineteen food types; diet variety, including berries and greens against scurvy, is needed for health.
Rising prosperity draws stronger raiders and foreign armies; difficulty is adjustable and pacifist mode removes them.
Palisades, stone walls, towers, barracks, and equipped soldiers.
Housing and the town center advance through tiers as prosperity and desirability grow.
Desirability from surroundings gates housing upgrades.
A tree of over 140 points of upgrades.
Crafted goods are traded for resources the town lacks.

games.name: Farthest Frontier
games.summary: A frontier-town city builder in which crop rotation, soil fertility, diet variety, clean water, and healers decide whether named diseases spread, while prosperity draws stronger raiders against walled defenses.

games.core_loop: scout and sign players -> set tactics and training -> the match engine simulates fixtures from attributes and instructions -> morale, form, and finances shift -> the board and fans judge results -> rebuild the squad over seasons
games.design_notes: Football Manager simulates the whole football world from a database of real players, staff, and clubs maintained by fan researchers, with tens of thousands of players developing, aging, and moving in loaded leagues. Matches are simulated from player attributes and tactical instructions and shown through a 2D engine in FM 2005 and a 3D engine from FM 2009. Information is uncertain: scouts and analysts reveal attributes and fit, and scout knowledge of an area is tracked (as 0 to 100 percent from FM 2018). Everton agreed in 2008 to use the database for scouting.
