One city-wide tax rate adds a positive offset to demand at low rates and a negative offset at high rates.
Police and fire stations write funding-scaled effect values to a block map that is smoothed outward.
Crime per cell is 128 - land value + density minus smoothed police effect, clamped 0-250.
Industry and traffic write a pollution map that depresses land value and can summon the monster.
Zones generate trips along roads; the resulting traffic density map adds to pollution and complaints.
Map windows show land value, crime, pollution, traffic density, police and fire coverage, and population density.
Fire, flood, tornado, earthquake, and a pollution-gated monster fire at 1/481, 1/241, or 1/61 per cycle by difficulty.
Time-limited scenarios such as Detroit 1972 set a goal to reach before the clock ends, added at Broderbund's suggestion.
A yearly evaluation turns problem scores into a 0-1000 rating and an approval poll.

games.name: SimCity
games.summary: The city builder in which a mayor zones residential, commercial, and industrial land, lays power and roads, and sets taxes while grid maps of land value, crime, pollution, and traffic drive where the city grows.

games.core_loop: shape terrain and zone light or dense residential, commercial, industrial land -> lay power lines, water pipes, roads, and rail -> demand and land value grow zones -> set per-zone tax rates, ordinances, and bonds -> fund schools, hospitals, police, and fire -> rebuild aging plants
games.design_notes: SimCity 2000 keeps the original's grid-map model but adds a second plane: an underground view for water pipes, subways, and road tunnels, so infrastructure is laid on a separate layer from zoning. Finance gains levers (three tax rates, ordinances, bonds), and most of the nine power plant types have limited lifespans, so replacement becomes a recurring capital cost. Yearly newspapers built from city state replace the score screen, and extreme deficit spending ends the game.

mechanics.note: Residential, commercial, and industrial zones in light and dense variants, plus seaport and airport zones.
Demand bars for residential, commercial, and industrial land, raised by connections to neighbor cities.
Nine plant types including wind, hydro, solar, fusion, and microwave; most have limited lifespans and must be rebuilt.
Yearly budget with department funding; extreme deficit spending ends the game.
Separate tax rates for residential, commercial, and industrial zones.
The player issues bonds to raise capital and pays interest on them.
City ordinances enacted for ongoing cost and effect.
An underground layer holds water pipes, subways, and road tunnels separate from the surface.
Water from pumps travels through underground pipes to zones.
Land has elevation that the player can raise or lower before and during play.
Schools, libraries, museums, hospitals, police, and fire stations cover surrounding zones.
Query tool shows land value per tile, which shapes development.
Query tool reports traffic on roads; highways and transit relieve it.
Disasters strike in play, and scenarios based on real cities stage specific ones.
Power plant types such as solar, fusion, and microwave and buildings such as arcologies become available in set invention years as the city's calendar advances.

games.name: SimCity 2000
games.summary: The isometric sequel to SimCity that adds terrain elevation, an underground layer of water pipes and subways, separate zone tax rates, bonds, ordinances, and power plants that age out.

games.core_loop: zone along roads -> GlassBox agents carry workers, goods, power, water, and sewage between buildings -> specialize the city in industries such as manufacturing, education, or tourism -> trade surpluses and share services with region neighbors -> pool resources into Great Works
games.design_notes: GlassBox replaces statistical maps with units that hold resource bins and agents that move resources between them, so a house holds a count of people and food, water travels as units, and traffic jams are the visible sum of commuting agents. Agents take the first available job and the first empty home rather than keeping persistent lives, and vehicles take the shortest route instead of the least loaded one, which players read as pathfinding errors. Cities were smaller than earlier games by design, and region play links them asynchronously through shared services, trade, and Great Works.

mechanics.note: Residential, commercial, and industrial zones are painted along roads; buildings develop inside them.
Sims go to the first job and first empty home they find; vehicles take the shortest route rather than the one with spare capacity.
Jams emerge from masses of commuting Sim agents on the road network.
Cities in a region connect by highway, rail, and water, trade resources, share services, and pool wealth into Great Works such as an arcology.
Power is carried as resource units from plants to buildings.
Water and sewage move as units through pipes between pumps, treatment, and buildings.
Map resources are mostly finite, though groundwater recharges.
A simulated global market raises and lowers prices of key resources with supply and demand.
Service buildings dispatch vehicle agents to calls.
Pollution and traffic cross city borders within a region.
Residents and businesses come in wealth levels with different demands.

games.name: SimCity (2013)
games.summary: A SimCity reboot built on the agent-based GlassBox engine, in which agents carry workers, power, water, and goods between buildings and small cities share a region over an always-online connection.

games.core_loop: terraform in God mode -> zone residential, commercial, industrial land at a density and connect roads -> wealth-level demand and desirability grow buildings -> set taxes and per-building service funding -> trade power, water, and garbage with neighbor cities -> grow the region
games.design_notes: SimCity 4 splits each zone type by wealth level, so demand and desirability are tracked per class and neighborhoods can decay or gentrify as conditions change. Cities of 1 to 4 km per side sit in a region and exchange water, electricity, and garbage disposal through neighbor deals, letting several specialized cities depend on each other; this single-player region has no exact match in the taxonomy (see run proposal). Its commute model drew praise from urban planner Jeff Speck, and the Building Architect Tool (2004) sustained a content community for over two decades.

mechanics.note: Residential, commercial, and industrial zones at low, medium, and high density, with agriculture as a separate industrial zone; buildings need road frontage.
Demand is reported separately for each wealth level of residents and for commercial and industrial subtypes.
Desirability is computed separately for each wealth level, so the same lot attracts different classes as services and nuisances change.
Commuters route trips over roads, rail, and transit; Rush Hour adds traffic flow tracing, avenues, and elevated rail.
Buildings belong to wealth levels and size stages; areas decay or gentrify.
Bus, subway, and rail stations carry commuters; Rush Hour adds elevated rail.
Civic buildings need ongoing funding set per building.
Tax rates per zone type and wealth level.
Schools, hospitals, police, and fire buildings cover areas; they lose output and gain maintenance cost as they age.
City ordinances with monthly costs and effects.
God mode reshapes terrain; most terraforming locks once a city is founded.
God mode triggers disasters on the city.
Mayor mode advisors comment on problems and suggest actions.
Industry and traffic pollute and reduce desirability.

games.name: SimCity 4
games.summary: A city builder in which several cities share a region map and trade utilities, while zones develop by density and wealth level and a commute model routes trips across roads and transit.

games.core_loop: set geological, atmospheric, and biological rates -> climate and biomes evolve -> taxa spread, mutate, and diversify -> one sapient species advances through seven ages -> pollution, war, and disasters feed back on climate -> spend energy on interventions
games.design_notes: Will Wright and Fred Haslam built SimEarth with James Lovelock as adviser, and its models encode Gaian feedback: volcanic dust cools the planet, warming melts ice caps and raises seas, and life alters atmospheric gas fractions shown to three decimal places. The player mostly acts through control panels that set rates such as continental drift, reproduction, and mutation, plus energy-priced interventions (50 units per terrain square, 500 per terraforming device), so play is closer to tuning coupled systems than to directing agents. Scenarios include Daisyworld, Lovelock's minimal model of temperature regulation by daisy color, and terraforming Mars and Venus.

mechanics.note: Atmospheric composition, temperature, ocean level, and biomes evolve together under Gaian feedback; volcanic dust cools, warming melts ice caps, extreme heat boils oceans, and Daisyworld reduces it to daisies regulating temperature.
Placing terrain, life, monoliths, oxygen generators, and terraforming devices costs energy (50 per terrain square, 500 per device) from a budget that grows with planetary development.

Taxa from prokaryotes to mammals spread and diversify by environment, with player-set reproduction and mutation rates; mass extinctions are often followed by renewed radiation, and any multicellular taxon can become sapient.
Mars, Venus, Ice Planet, and Dune scenarios ask the player to make hostile planets habitable.
Hurricanes, wildfires, earthquakes, tsunamis, and meteors occur, with disease and pollution scaling with population.

games.name: SimEarth
games.summary: A planetary god game built on James Lovelock's Gaia hypothesis in which geology, atmosphere, climate, life, and civilization models interact over billions of years under the player's parameter changes and interventions.

games.core_loop: design species genes and world physics -> plants grow and animals eat, breed, and mutate -> populations boom, crash, or go extinct -> read graphs -> edit genes or environment and run again
games.design_notes: Designed by Ken Karakotsios, SimLife moves the player's control point down to the genome: plant and animal species are edited gene by gene, and the world's physical parameters can be changed, so the toy is about running ecological and evolutionary experiments rather than pursuing goals. Where SimEarth aggregates taxa into planetary stocks, SimLife works at the scale of a landscape and its individual species, mixing exclusive designed animals such as the Killer Penguin and Monkeyphant with player-made ones. Direct gene editing matches the genome-modification proposal from run catalog-ge.

mechanics.note: The player edits the genetics of plant and animal species directly, and offspring inherit those genes with variation.
Evolution is simulated and can be steered; species whose genes fit the designed environment persist while others decline.
Designed ecosystems pair plant species with the animals that eat them, so gene edits ripple through who can feed on whom.
Players create and modify worlds and environments as well as species.

games.name: SimLife
games.summary: A Maxis artificial-life toy in which the player edits plant and animal genes, landscape, and the world's physical parameters, then watches food chains and evolution play out.

games.core_loop: build floors, lobbies, and elevators -> place offices, condos, hotels, and shops -> tenants travel by elevator on daily routines -> long waits raise stress and drive tenants out -> rent and population raise the star rating -> unlock new facilities
games.design_notes: SimTower turns a building into a vertical transit problem: standard elevators span up to 30 floors and express elevators the full height, so the player designs shafts, sky lobbies, and stops to keep queues short as the tower grows toward 100 floors above ground and 9 below. Tenant stress, not money alone, gates the star rating from one to five and finally the Tower rating, which needs a cathedral on top. Events such as a terrorist bomb ransom, VIP visits that can unlock a star, fires, and pests interrupt the routine.

mechanics.note: Tenants wait at elevator lobbies; long waits raise stress, and stressed tenants move out.
Floors and tenant units are placed on a side-view grid; tenant type and position set elevator demand.
Office workers, residents, shoppers, and hotel guests travel at different times of day, creating rush periods at lobbies.
Population and conditions advance the tower from one to five stars and then to Tower status, each step unlocking facility types.
Up to 100 floors above ground and 9 below; standard elevators span 30 floors, express elevators the full height.
People route between floors by elevators, escalators, and stairs.
Rent and sales income fund construction.
Terrorist bomb threats with a ransom or search, fires, and pest infestations.

games.name: SimTower
games.summary: A skyscraper management game in which the player stacks offices, condos, hotels, and shops and designs elevator service so tenants on daily routines do not wait long enough to stress out and leave.

games.core_loop: take a delivery or repair task -> pick truck, tires, and attachments -> drive into deforming mud, snow, or water -> recover when stuck -> deliver cargo -> earn money and rank -> unlock upgrades and new trucks
games.design_notes: Terrain is the antagonist: mud, snow, and water respond to vehicle weight, speed, and momentum, so route choice and tire type matter more than speed, and optional timed contests pay more for faster completion. The physics engine is the one Pavel Zagrebelnyy built for MudRunner, the sequel to Spintires. Mechanical upgrades such as snorkels and chain tires are gated behind progress thresholds, and up to four players can share a map.

mechanics.note: Mud, snow, and water react to each truck's weight, speed, and momentum, so ground conditions change as vehicles pass and can bog down underpowered or wrongly fitted trucks.
Tire types, frame attachments, and accessories such as exhaust snorkels for deep water and chain tires for snow change how each of over 60 trucks copes with terrain.
Missions deliver cargo or complete construction and repair jobs; optional timed contests pay more the faster they are finished.
Damage is shown on the vehicle model and in the interface and must be repaired.
Mechanical upgrades require reaching a progress threshold.

games.name: SnowRunner
games.summary: An off-road trucking sim in which the player hauls cargo across mud, snow, and water whose surfaces deform under each truck's weight and tires, upgrading a fleet to reach harder terrain.

games.core_loop: lay out houses, streets, and workshops -> tens of thousands of citizens and slaves work, worship, and seek their desires -> appoint nobles to run the realm -> supply and train armies -> fight real-time battles -> trade, ally, or conquer neighboring kingdoms
games.design_notes: Songs of Syx scales individual simulation to city size: each of tens of thousands of citizens and slaves has a race, religion, fears, and desires, and each soldier in battles of up to 50,000 units needs supplies. Nobles can be appointed or imported to manage the kingdom but may try to usurp the player. The game has been in early access since September 2020 with no fixed 1.0 date.

mechanics.note: Citizens and slaves of several races, each with distinct needs, religion, and roles.
Real-time battles of up to 50,000 individual units commanded by the player.
Each citizen's needs and desires drive behavior.
Tens of thousands of agents path through streets to work and services.
Every soldier must be supplied.
Alliances, trade, and war with other kingdoms.
Appointed nobles may try to usurp the ruler.

games.name: Songs of Syx
games.summary: A low-fantasy city builder in which tens of thousands of individually simulated citizens and slaves of several races live in a growing city-state whose armies of up to 50,000 units fight real-time battles.

games.core_loop: mine ore from voxel asteroids and planets -> refine and assemble components -> weld blocks into ship or station grids -> power and pilot under inertia -> collide, fight, or deform -> repair and redesign
games.design_notes: Space Engineers treats a ship as a grid of blocks where each block has mass, inertia, and hit points, and functional blocks (thrusters per direction, gyroscopes, reactors, cockpits) decide whether it can move at all; there is no ship stat sheet apart from the blocks. Collisions and weapons deform or destroy individual blocks, and terrain is editable voxels, so construction, mining, and damage share one physical model. Survival mode adds a refine-assemble production chain and suit oxygen and energy, and an in-game programmable block lets players automate ships with scripts.

mechanics.note: Ships and stations are small or large grids of armor and functional blocks; thrusters only push along their facing, so thrust coverage on each axis, gyroscope count, and power supply decide handling.
Volumetric physics gives every block mass and inertia; ships drift under Newtonian motion with optional inertia dampeners, and gravity generators and planets pull loose objects.
Asteroid and planet voxels can be drilled and carved, and armor blocks deform or break block by block under collisions and weapon fire.
Hand drills and ship drills mine ore from voxel deposits.
Refineries turn ore into ingots and assemblers turn ingots into components for welding.
Conveyor blocks connect inventories so refineries, assemblers, and cargo containers move items automatically, with sorters filtering flow.
Reactors, solar panels, batteries, and hydrogen engines feed every functional block on a grid; unpowered blocks stop.
The programmable block runs player-written C# scripts that read and command blocks on the grid.
Sensors, timer blocks, and event controllers trigger block actions without code.
In survival the suit tracks health, energy, oxygen, and hydrogen.
Air vents pressurize sealed rooms with oxygen; breaches depressurize them.
Grids save as blueprints that a projector block displays for welding and that are shared on Steam Workshop.
A C# modding API, Workshop, and mod.io support custom blocks and logic.
Each block has hit points, and damaged functional blocks such as thrusters, reactors, and gyroscopes stop working until welded back.

games.name: Space Engineers
games.summary: A voxel sandbox where players mine asteroids and planets and build ships and stations block by block, with every block carrying mass, inertia, power needs, and damage under Newtonian physics.

games.core_loop: build the ship tile by tile -> balance oxygen, CO2, temperature, and power -> crew work and meet needs -> jump through hyperspace to a new sector -> mine, salvage derelicts, trade, or fight factions -> grow the ship and crew
games.design_notes: Bugbyte describes it as combining RimWorld-style emergent storytelling with a tile-based gas simulation, and names RimWorld, Dwarf Fortress, Spacebase DF-9, and Oxygen Not Included as inspirations. The ship is both the base and the vehicle, so layout choices (a bed beside the ship core disrupts sleep) and life support are coupled to combat, where fire, smoke, gas, and hull breaches cascade through the same simulation. Early access began in May 2020 and 1.0 shipped in May 2026.

mechanics.note: Each tile holds gas quantities; life support modules produce oxygen and remove CO2, and hazardous gases from facilities, fires, or explosions spread until scrubbed or vented.
Hull, walls, doors, and facilities are placed freely tile by tile to form the ship, which can be expanded or rebuilt at any time.
Crew needs for food, sleep, comfort, safety, and friends drive mood, alongside conditions such as starvation or feeling unhygienic.
Neglected crew suffer mental breaks ranging from starting fights to venting other crew into space.
Thermal regulators keep compartments at comfortable temperatures.
Power nodes distribute electricity across the ship.
Crew relationships added in 2022.
Standing with pirates, slavers, merchants, cults, and android factions.
Asteroids are mined for raw materials.
Raw materials are refined into building materials.
Crew are drafted and equipped for ground combat and away missions.
Fire and smoke spread through damaged compartments.
Each playthrough generates a new galaxy of sectors, stations, and ships.

games.name: Space Haven
games.summary: A spaceship colony sim in which the player builds a ship tile by tile and keeps a crew with needs, moods, and relationships alive inside a tile-based simulation of oxygen, CO2, heat, and power.

claims.text: Barth's earlier Flash game The Codex of Alchemical Engineering (2008), which is not in this dataset, is the documented precursor of SpaceChem's manipulator puzzles.

games.core_loop: read the input and output molecules -> place waldo paths and instruction icons in a 10x8 reactor -> run and debug collisions -> meet the output quota -> compare cycles, reactors, and instructions on histograms -> optimize or move on
games.design_notes: SpaceChem made the program itself the factory: each 10x8 reactor holds two waldos, red and blue, programmed independently or synchronized by instruction icons laid on the grid, and multiple reactors connect on a planet-surface pipeline so one reactor's output feeds another. Execution is deterministic, so a solution either produces the quota or deadlocks or collides, and success is followed by global histograms of cycles, reactors, and instructions that Zach Barth designed to show where a solution sits without the intimidation of a ranked leaderboard. Each planet ends in a defense level where production must keep pace with an attacker. Barth expanded the manipulator puzzles of his 2008 Flash game The Codex of Alchemical Engineering, and the instruction-grid plus histogram template recurs across Zachtronics' later games. ResearchNet let players share puzzles.

mechanics.note: Two waldos per reactor, red and blue, follow player-placed paths and instruction icons that pick up, rotate, drop, bond, and route atoms, programmed independently or synchronized, with deterministic and visible execution.
A solution passes when it outputs the required molecule quota and is then scored on cycles, number of reactors, and number of instructions used.
After completion the player's cycles, reactors, and instructions are plotted on global histograms of other players' solutions, chosen over a ranked leaderboard to avoid discouraging players.

Reactors placed on a larger planet map pass molecules through pipelines, so later puzzles split a synthesis across several reactors, some limited to tasks such as breaking bonds, with fission and fusion nodes.
Each puzzle fixes inputs, target outputs, available reactor types, and quotas; defense levels add a time pressure from an attacking enemy.
ResearchNet distributes user-made puzzles that other players download and solve.

games.name: SpaceChem
games.summary: A programming puzzle game in which the player lays out instruction paths for two waldos in grid reactors that grab, bond, rotate, and split atoms into target molecules, with each solution scored on cycles, reactors, and instructions against global histograms.

claims.text: The free Proof of Concept Demo Alpha 0.4.0 was publicly released on 2012-05-27, and the game entered Steam Early Access on 2018-09-28 without a later 1.0 release.
The developer is credited only by the handle Quasar on Steam and the development blog; no personal name was found in the sources checked.

games.core_loop: creatures feed, pay energy costs, and reproduce -> offspring genomes mutate -> environment and rovers decide who eats and who starves -> trait averages drift and lineages split into species -> player edits genes, climate, or triggers ice ages and floods -> watch the clade diagram branch
games.design_notes: Species, built by a single developer known as Quasar, simulates evolution with no fitness function: genes are numbers, most mutations add a random value in [-1, 1] scaled by a background mutation rate and radiation, and survival is whatever the body and environment allow. Energy costs come from analyzing each creature's skeleton for internal forces and torques, so morphology has a physical price, and creatures can eat only what their head reaches. Species are not predefined: a species is a population that can interbreed within a genetic distance, and it splits only when intermediate forms die out, which the clade diagram records. Species defined at runtime by genetic distance are not yet a mechanic in the taxonomy (proposal runtime-speciation). A free alpha (0.4.0) was public from 2012, and the Steam Early Access build from 2018 has not reached 1.0.

mechanics.note: Each creature's body and behavior come from numeric genes; offspring are randomly modified copies of one or more parents, with most mutations a random value in [-1, 1] times a modifier for background mutation rate and radiation.
No fitness score exists; creatures that cannot pay skeleton-derived energy costs, reach food, or tolerate local climate fail to reproduce, so trait averages drift and lineages speciate.
Climate varies across the map, and climate control devices create local cold, hot, fertile, or dead ground.
The player triggers ice ages and world floods, programs rovers to feed or kill creatures by genetic distance to a target genome, and edits genomes in an isolated nursery.
Creature inspection shows each individual's DNA and stats.
Species averages over time, a clade diagram (Tree of Life), a satellite range map, and a web-of-life view of genetic variety.

games.name: Species: Artificial Life, Real Evolution
games.summary: A solo-developed evolution simulator in which creatures defined by numeric genes mutate, breed, and speciate in real time across a 3D world while the player observes, edits the gene pool, and alters climate.

games.core_loop: eat to earn DNA points -> edit body parts to change abilities -> befriend or fight other species -> stage completes and grants consequence traits -> next stage changes the rules -> colonize and terraform planets -> creations upload to the Sporepedia and populate other players' galaxies
games.design_notes: Spore's evolution is player design rather than selection: body parts bought with DNA points set speed, attack, and social abilities directly, and nothing is inherited by differential survival. Its distinctive system is the part-based editors (18 share one interface) whose creations are stored as compact descriptions of a few kilobytes and reconstructed procedurally, which let Maxis upload every creation and redistribute them as the inhabitants of other players' galaxies (over 100 million by May 2009). Each of the five stages swaps in a different genre's rules, and play style in each stage assigns consequence traits that carry forward.

mechanics.note: Creature, building, and vehicle editors assemble parts such as mouths, legs, and arms whose choice sets abilities, diet options, and stats; textures and animation are applied procedurally to the assembled topology.
Every creation uploads automatically to the Sporepedia and is redistributed to populate other players' worlds, so other players' designs fill the galaxy without manual import.

Each stage ends at a progress threshold and hands the species to a new rule set (cell, creature, tribal, civilization, space), with three consequence traits awarded from how aggressive or social the player was.
The player directly steers the cell, the creature, and later a spaceship.
Tribal and civilization stages switch to commanding up to 12 tribe members, then vehicles and cities.
Creature-stage species, tribes, nations, and space empires such as the Grox can be befriended through social actions or conquered.
In the space stage rocky planets can be terraformed, their ecosystems changed, and features such as mountains and lakes added.

games.name: Spore
games.summary: A five-stage game in which the player guides a species from cell to galactic empire, building its body, vehicles, and buildings in part-based editors whose creations are shared automatically through the Sporepedia.

games.core_loop: plan the day -> spend energy watering, harvesting, mining, or fishing -> sell crops and artisan goods -> buy seeds, tools, and buildings -> gift and talk to villagers -> complete Community Center bundles -> new areas and seasons open
games.design_notes: Eric Barone built Stardew Valley alone over about five years in response to Harvest Moon, keeping its seasonal crop calendar and town relationships while leaving the long-term structure open-ended. Each day is bounded by an energy bar refilled each morning and a clock that forces sleep, so play is a daily allocation problem across farming, foraging, fishing, mining, and socializing. Friendship is a point stock (250 points per heart, 10 hearts for most villagers) that loses 2 points per day without conversation and accepts two gifts per week, with birthday gifts worth eight times as much. Community Center bundles make collection the main progression gate.

mechanics.note: Seasonal seeds need daily watering (rain or sprinklers substitute) and grow through stages over set day counts; most crops must be harvested before the season changes.
Four 28-day seasons gate which crops grow, which fish and forage appear, and which festivals occur.
An energy bar refills each morning, drains with tool use, and is restored by food; the clock forces bed by 2 a.m. or the player passes out and loses money.

Each villager has a friendship stock of 250 points per heart up to 10 hearts; it decays 2 points per day without talking, takes two gifts a week, multiplies birthday gifts by 8, and unlocks heart events.
Community Center bundles ask for sets of crops, forage, fish, and artisan goods; completed rooms repair town infrastructure and unlock areas, and the museum collects minerals and artifacts.
Barns and coops house animals that produce eggs, milk, and wool when fed and cared for; animals cannot be slaughtered.
Twelve marriage candidates regardless of player gender; spouses help with chores, and couples can have children.
Farming, foraging, fishing, mining, and combat levels rise with practice and unlock recipes and professions.
Kegs, preserves jars, and other machines convert crops and animal products into higher-value artisan goods over fixed processing times.
Crops and animal products come in normal, silver, gold, and iridium quality.
A help-wanted board posts item, fishing, and slaying requests from townspeople.
Recipes turn gathered materials into sprinklers, fences, machines, and bombs.
Villagers follow routines that vary by weekday, season, and weather.
Rain waters crops and changes fish and villager routines.

games.name: Stardew Valley
games.summary: A farming and life sim in which the player restores an inherited farm over four 28-day seasons, splitting a daily energy budget among crops, animals, mining, fishing, and friendships with Pelican Town's residents.

games.core_loop: land with a starter kit -> mine and smelt ore -> build an airtight frame -> pipe, filter, and heat a breathable atmosphere -> power and automate with logic chips -> expand while fixing pressure, fire, and temperature failures
games.design_notes: The atmosphere is the main simulated system: each sealed volume and pipe network carries a mix of gases with temperature and pressure, so heating a room raises its pressure, mixing fuel and oxygen can burn or explode, and a pressure difference across a wall can blow it out. Survival needs are deliberately front-loaded; later play is building plant that keeps the atmosphere stable, then automating it with IC10 chips programmed in an assembly language. The game has been in early access since 2017.

mechanics.note: Rooms and pipe networks hold mixtures of oxygen, nitrogen, carbon dioxide, volatiles, pollutants, and water with pressure and temperature; gases mix, and combustion consumes fuel and oxygen and releases heat.
Gas temperature changes pressure and habitability; radiators, heat exchangers, heaters, and coolers move heat between pipes, rooms, and the planet's atmosphere.
Pipes, pumps, filtration units, mixers, and regulators route gases between devices; pipes and tanks fail when pressure exceeds their rating.
Early survival requires breathable gas, food, water, and suit temperature; suits carry tanks and filters until a habitat is sealed.
Solar panels, generators, and batteries feed cable networks; overloaded cables burn out.
IC10 chips run player-written assembly that reads and writes device logic values such as pressure and temperature.
Logic readers, writers, memory, and sensors chain devices without code.
Ore is mined from deformable voxel terrain.
Furnaces and arc furnaces smelt ore into ingots, and autolathes and other fabricators turn ingots into kits.
Hydroponic plants need light, water, and suitable gases, and exchange carbon dioxide for oxygen.
Walls hold limited pressure differences; exceeding them causes fatigue and explosive decompression.
Frames, walls, pipes, and devices are placed on a grid piece by piece, and placement decides airtightness.

games.name: Stationeers
games.summary: A first-person space station survival game whose core is an atmospheric simulation of gas mixtures, pressure, temperature, and combustion that the player must engineer with pipes, power, and programmable logic.

games.core_loop: survey systems with science ships -> claim systems and colonize planets -> build districts that create jobs for pops -> draw research cards and build fleets -> negotiate or fight neighboring empires -> survive the late-game crisis
games.design_notes: Stellaris combines a space 4X opening (survey, claim, colonize) with Paradox grand strategy systems: real time with pause, internal factions, and event chains. Its research model replaces a visible tree with weighted random card draws, so two runs of the same empire research in different orders. Hyperlane-only travel turns the galaxy into a graph with chokepoints. Henrik Fahraeus named Star Control II, Master of Orion II, and Europa Universalis IV as roughly equal influences.

mechanics.note: Physics, society, and engineering research each offer three semi-random project cards weighted by ethics, the scientist's traits, and known technologies; rare technologies and anomaly-granted cards vary each run, and costs rise as the game goes on.

Pops fill jobs created by planetary districts and buildings in worker, specialist, and ruler strata; each job consumes and produces resources such as energy, minerals, food, consumer goods, and alloys.
Anomalies found by science ships open authored event chains, and galactic crises such as marauder invasions, awakened machine empires, and extradimensional invaders begin after set periods.
Empires negotiate, form federations, and go to war; ethics such as xenophobe or xenophile shape AI attitudes.
Pops join political factions according to ethics, and faction support produces unity.
Planets beyond the core limit can be grouped into sectors run by AI governors with a player-set focus.
Ships are designed from hull sections and components.
Each galaxy is generated with star systems linked only by hyperlanes.
Species traits and leader traits modify output and behavior.
Ethics, civics, policies, and edicts change empire rules.
Unity, produced partly by faction support, buys traditions, and influence pays for new outposts and territorial claims.
Empire size grows with systems, colonies, and pops, and size beyond administrative capacity raises technology and tradition costs; bureaucrat jobs add capacity to offset it.
Each pop holds an ethic that drifts toward ethics with higher attraction, modified by government ethics, policies, and living conditions, and pop ethics decide faction membership.
Empires take systems by building outposts, borders follow owned systems, and claims bought with influence set what wars can take.
War exhaustion rises from losses and occupation, and a side at maximum exhaustion can be forced into a status quo peace.
Fleet battles resolve from ship weapons, shields, armor, and hull values against each other, and ground combat compares army attack and health.

games.name: Stellaris
games.summary: A real-time-with-pause space 4X and grand strategy game in which the player designs a species and empire, expands across a procedurally generated hyperlane galaxy from 2200, manages pops, jobs, ethics-based factions, and research card draws, and faces late-game crises.

games.core_loop: dive from the lifepod -> gather resources and recover blueprints -> craft tools, vehicles, and base modules -> manage oxygen, food, and water -> dive deeper into new biomes and story sites -> build the means to escape the planet
games.design_notes: Included as a boundary case: the map, story, and progression are hand-authored, and the simulated layer is a set of survival meters plus base power and fauna behavior. Oxygen is the distinctive meter because it ties survival to depth and distance from air, making range a resource. Mode settings remove meters to change genre: Freedom drops hunger and thirst, Creative drops all depleting stats, and Hardcore adds permanent death without low-oxygen warnings.

mechanics.note: Health, hunger, thirst, and oxygen deplete in Survival mode; oxygen limits each dive's depth and duration, Freedom mode removes hunger and thirst, and Creative removes all depleting stats.
Gathered resources are crafted into tools, base parts, and submersibles from blueprints the player has recovered.
Bases are assembled from placed modules.
Bases and vehicles need energy sources.
A day-night cycle and frequent eclipses change visibility.
Cooked fish spoils over time; cured fish does not.
Optional in Hardcore mode.

games.name: Subnautica
games.summary: An underwater survival game on an ocean planet where the player manages oxygen, food, and water while crafting tools, submersibles, and bases to explore deeper and escape.

claims.text: Suck Up! was publicly playable through Proxima's own launcher before its Steam 1.0 release on 2025-10-01; the site's terms, last updated 2023-12-05, already metered AI-model use in tokens, and the site calls the launcher build early access.

games.core_loop: pick a disguise -> knock on a resident's door -> speak a pitch aloud -> the model replies in character and weighs trust -> get invited in and feed, or get refused -> next house
games.design_notes: At runtime a language model plays each resident: the player's spoken words go to a hosted model (the Steam page lists ChatGPT from OpenAI; the December 2023 terms name GPT 3.5 and Llama 2 and meter use in tokens) along with the resident's authored personality, and its reply, delivered in voiced audio, decides whether the player has earned entry. The challenge is social engineering against a model that has been told to be suspicious, so disguises (knight, superhero, a previous victim) work as context that changes the model's judgment. Players author new residents' personalities and whole neighborhoods and share them on Steam Workshop. It is a boundary case: the persuasion is judged by the model rather than by a simulated social state.

mechanics.note: The player talks to residents with a real microphone, and the store page says responses depend on tone and strategy.
A hosted language model (ChatGPT from OpenAI per the store page) generates each resident's reply and in-character decision in real time from its personality prompt and the conversation.
Each resident has an authored personality and behaviors that condition the model, and players can write their own.
Steam Workshop shares player-made characters and full neighborhoods.
Modes include Love Bites (split up couples at a Valentine's Day party) and Mic Drop (rap battles against characters).

games.name: Suck Up!
games.summary: A voice-controlled comedy game in which the player, as a disguised vampire, talks AI-driven townspeople into letting them inside, with each resident's replies generated by a language model from its personality and the player's words.

games.core_loop: pick a procedure -> move the hand and press finger keys to grab tools -> cut, break, and remove body parts -> place the new organ -> keep Bob alive -> score and time
games.design_notes: Made in 48 hours at the 2013 Global Game Jam, the game turns control difficulty into the content: the mouse moves the hand, a mouse button rotates or lowers it, and A, W, E, R, and Space close individual fingers, a scheme modeled on Jurassic Park: Trespasser. Tools and organs are rigid bodies, so most outcomes come from collisions and dropped objects rather than authored surgical steps. Medicine is a comic frame with a thin vital-sign model; a heart rate at zero requires charging the defibrillators. Included as a boundary case for embodied control.

mechanics.note: The mouse moves the hand, holding the right button rotates it, the left button lowers it, and A, W, E, R, and Space each close one finger, so grasping a scalpel is itself the challenge.
Instruments, organs, and bones are physics objects that collide, slip, and fall, so most mistakes are physical accidents rather than authored failure states.
Damage to the patient drives a small vital-sign model; when heart rate reaches 0 the player must charge the defibrillators.
Procedures such as heart and kidney transplants are replayed in an operating room, a bouncing ambulance, and zero gravity.

games.name: Surgeon Simulator
games.summary: A physics comedy surgery game in which the player controls one hand with separate finger keys to perform transplants on the patient Bob before his vital signs fail.

games.core_loop: land rockets with drones and prefabs -> drones build power, water, and oxygen infrastructure -> build domes and bring colonists from Earth -> colonists' traits, comfort, and sanity drive work and stability -> research and export rare metals for funding -> weather disasters and Mysteries
games.design_notes: Surviving Mars splits construction from population: drones working within range of hubs build and maintain everything, and colonists arrive only after domes have power, water, and oxygen. Colonists carry traits, flaws, and specializations and track morale, comfort, sanity, and health, so dome services decide whether they work, turn Earthsick, or rebel. Mysteries layer authored storylines (plagues, rival corporations, AI revolts, alien contact) on top of disasters such as dust storms, meteors, and cold waves.

mechanics.note: Generators and batteries feed cable networks to domes and buildings; a dome without power, water, or oxygen cannot sustain colonists.
Water and oxygen travel by pipe from extractors and producers to domes.
Drones within a hub's range carry resources, build, and maintain buildings.
Research spans physics, engineering, social, biotechnology, and robotics fields.
Drone hubs and dome services serve within a range.
Colonists have traits, flaws, and specializations that suit them to jobs.
Comfort, sanity, health, and morale change with services and events.
Unhappy colonists may become Earthsick or rebels.
Dust storms, meteor storms, cold waves, and dust devils.
Buildings need drone maintenance to keep working.
Green Planet (2019) adds terraforming of atmosphere, temperature, and water.
Mysteries run storylines such as plagues, rival corporations, AI revolts, and alien contact.
Metals, rare metals, concrete, and water are extracted; rare metal exports fund imports.

games.name: Surviving Mars
games.summary: A Mars colony city builder in which drones build power, water, and oxygen networks before colonists with traits arrive in domes, while research, Earth sponsors, and dust storms, meteors, and cold waves shape survival.

games.core_loop: read briefings and dialogue -> choose responses and policy decisions -> budget, alignment, and story flags update -> later options open or close -> reach an ending and a political-compass result
games.design_notes: Suzerain is mostly authored text, about 450,000 words, in which choices are recorded as state: the budget and accumulated decisions gate later dialogue options and endings. It is a boundary case included for how a political game can run on dilemma choices and state-gated story branches rather than an equation network. The ending screen places the player on an in-universe political compass computed from choices made across the term.

mechanics.note: Ministers, advisers, and family members present situations as dialogue, and multiple-choice responses on constitutional reform, economic model, security, and welfare trade off budget, alignment, and later options.
Story chapters branch on recorded choices, opening or closing later scenes and deciding which ending the term reaches.
Available budget and resources are shown and drawn down by decisions.
Sordland can side with the western or eastern bloc or stay neutral, and deals with its neighbor Rumburg.
Major choices set constitutional reforms and a market-driven or centrally planned economy.
Ministers and advisers brief the president and argue positions.

games.name: Suzerain
games.summary: A text-based political narrative game in which the player, as newly elected President Anton Rayne of Sordland, makes dialogue and policy choices across one term that shift the budget, foreign alignment, and constitutional reform toward one of several endings.

games.core_loop: pet calls for attention -> feed a meal or snack, play, scold, clean, or give medicine -> meters and care history accumulate -> pet ages after each sleep -> care history selects its next form -> it lives on or dies
games.design_notes: Aki Maita and Akihiro Yokoi reduced a pet to three meters (Hunger, Happy, Training) plus droppings and sickness on a three-button LCD device that runs continuously; early units could pause only through the clock settings. Meals fill Hunger, snacks and a minigame raise Happy but excess snacks cause illness, scolding when the pet calls for attention fills Training, and uncleaned droppings lead to sickness shown by a skull. Each life stage lasts a set number of days and age advances when the pet wakes, and care quality selects the adult character, turning care history into a visible outcome (proposed as care-dependent-development).

mechanics.note: Care actions are meal, snack, game, scold, clean, and medicine; meals are limited by fullness while snacks are not, and excess snacks cause sickness.
Hunger and Happy meters, shown as hearts, deplete over real time and are refilled by meals, snacks, and the minigame.
The pet lives on the device clock set at hatching and sleeps nightly; time keeps passing between check-ins.
Baby, Child, Teenager, Adult, and Special stages (plus Senior in some models) each last a set number of days, with age advancing on waking; old age eventually ends its life.
Poor care, sickness, or old age kills the pet; the A and C buttons start a new egg.
A nightly sleep period suspends care demands and marks age increments.
The device beeps and shows an attention icon when the pet needs care or calls for discipline.
Care quality during each life stage, such as unanswered calls, overfeeding snacks, and uncleaned droppings, selects the next form, so the same egg can grow into different adult characters.

games.name: Tamagotchi
games.summary: A 1996 keychain virtual pet whose hunger, happiness, and training meters run on a real-time clock, and whose care quality determines which adult form it grows into and how long it lives.

games.core_loop: survey the level -> cut, blast, and ram a route through voxel structures -> stage vehicles and ramps -> trigger the alarm by taking a target -> grab the rest along the planned path before the timer ends
games.design_notes: Every object is made of small voxels with material types (wood, plaster, brick, metal, glass), and disconnected chunks become rigid bodies that fall, roll, and burn, so geometry is a resource the player spends. The design separates an unlimited planning phase from a timed execution phase: picking up a connected target starts a 60-second alarm, so the player engineers shortcuts with tools, explosives, and vehicles before the first grab. Materials resist tools differently, and fire spreads through wood, which turns construction knowledge into route planning.

mechanics.note: Levels are made of small voxels whose material sets which tools can break them; the sledgehammer breaks soft materials, the blowtorch cuts metal, and explosives remove volumes.
Voxel chunks cut loose become dynamic bodies with mass that fall, roll, and crush; vehicles and cranes push and lift them.
In most heists taking an alarmed target starts a 60-second timer to reach the getaway vehicle, so the route must be prepared during an unlimited setup phase.
Fire spreads across wood and other flammables and can burn targets or open routes; burning structures weaken and fall.
Materials respond differently to each tool and to fire; a fire extinguisher puts fires out.
Sections cut off from all supports fall, so removing pillars can drop a floor.
40 campaign missions specify targets, optional targets, and conditions such as stealing, destroying, or collecting evidence.
Lua scripting, a level editor, and Steam Workshop support custom levels, tools, and modes.

games.name: Teardown
games.summary: A heist and destruction game set in fully destructible voxel levels where the player plans a route by cutting, smashing, and driving through structures, then races a 60-second alarm timer to grab the targets.

games.core_loop: place wind turbines on rock -> power toxin scrubbers that clean soil -> irrigate and pump water into riverbeds -> upgrade to grow wetlands, meadows, and forest -> attract animals and restore weather -> recycle every building and leave
games.design_notes: It inverts the city-builder loop: growth is measured in restored tiles rather than population, and points earned per restored tile are the only currency for further buildings, so efficient placement compounds. The final step requires recycling all infrastructure to build an airship and leave, so a layout must be removable as well as productive. Subgenre is set to city-builder because its lineage is placement and budget puzzles rather than population or evolution modeling. It began as a Ludum Dare 45 entry in October 2019.

mechanics.note: Buildings have placement rules: wind turbines go only on stone tiles and power toxin scrubbers, which clean soil so irrigators can green it.
Each restored tile earns points, and points are the only currency for buildings and upgrades, so a map can stall if spending outruns restoration.
Pumps refill dried riverbeds and tools carve new rivers.
Tools create new rivers and some stone tiles.
Restored biomes attract deer, birds, fish, and bears.
Each map sets restoration targets before the player can recycle buildings and leave.

games.name: Terra Nil
games.summary: A reverse city builder in which the player places machines to clean toxic soil, restore water, and grow biomes on a barren map, then recycles every building and leaves.

claims.text: Early access began on 2023-02-10, and version 1.0 released on 2025-10-10 with multiple drones and a revamped tech tree, published by Metaroot.

games.core_loop: write a drone program -> execute it on the farm grid -> plant, water, and harvest crops -> spend harvests on unlocks -> new language features and crops change what code is worth writing -> optimize for speed and leaderboard times
games.design_notes: The Farmer Was Replaced teaches programming by making farm labor too slow to do any other way: the drone does nothing unless code tells it to, and the language itself is unlocked piecemeal (loops, variables, functions, lists, dictionaries) with farm expansion and new crops. Execution is metered in simulated ticks rather than real CPU: literals and assignment are free, arithmetic and getters cost 1 tick, and a successful move() costs 200, so optimization means reducing drone actions more than reducing statements. Crops add algorithmic puzzles: polyculture companions requested within three moves multiply yield, harvesting the sunflower with the most petals (out of at least ten) gives eight times the power that doubles drone speed, and mazes and dinosaurs need search-style code. Leaderboards run the player's program as fixed-start simulations totaling at least two hours and score the average time. Code lives in .py files that external editors can edit.

mechanics.note: A Python-like language stored in .py files drives the drone; every operation has a tick cost (arithmetic 1, a successful move 200, a failed action 1) that scales with the speed factor, and Megafarm adds more drones.
Grass, bushes, trees, carrots, pumpkins, cactus, and sunflowers are planted, grown, and harvested by the drone, with Watering and Fertilizer unlocks that act on growth.
Harvested resources buy unlocks with prerequisites, including farm expansion, speed, loops, variables, functions, lists, dictionaries, polyculture, mazes, dinosaurs, and the leaderboard.

Under polyculture, grass, bushes, trees, and carrots request a different companion plant on a tile within three moves, found with get_companion(); planting it multiplies yield, 5x before upgrades and doubling per upgrade.
Leaderboards run the player's program from fixed starts until a resource target is met, repeated to at least two hours, and score the average completion time.
Every operation costs simulated ticks (arithmetic 1, a successful move() 200, a failed action 1), so optimizing means cutting drone actions more than statements.

games.name: The Farmer Was Replaced
games.summary: A programming game in which the player writes Python-like code for a farming drone on a grid farm, where every operation costs simulated ticks, and harvests crops to buy unlocks for language features, farm size, more drones, and new crops.

games.core_loop: read the puzzle goal -> place the supplied parts among fixed objects -> start the machine -> watch the chain reaction -> adjust positions until the goal triggers
games.design_notes: Each puzzle fixes some objects in a side-view scene and hands the player a small inventory of parts; the solution is a chain reaction where each part triggers the next, such as a ball dropping on a seesaw that frees a mouse that runs toward cheese. The physics engine models gravity and air pressure as global settings and has no random number generator, so a design behaves the same on every run and solutions are verifiable. A freeform mode exposes all parts so players can make puzzles for others.

mechanics.note: Levels supply a limited inventory of parts such as balls, ropes, pulleys, belts, electrical generators, cats, and mice that the player places among fixed objects; parts act on each other by contact, rope, or belt.
A deterministic 2D physics engine with no random number generator moves balls, seesaws, and falling objects under level-set gravity and air pressure, so the same design always gives the same run.
Each puzzle states one simple goal, such as moving an object to a target, that must be met with only the parts provided.
Some parts react to others by fixed rules, such as a mouse running toward cheese.
Electrical generators driven by other parts power electrical devices in the contraption.
Freeform mode saves player-built puzzles, using any part, for others to solve.

games.name: The Incredible Machine
games.summary: A Rube Goldberg puzzle game in which the player places supplied parts such as balls, ropes, pulleys, belts, and animals into a level so that a deterministic physics run completes a simple goal.

games.core_loop: explore a frozen region -> scavenge, hunt, and harvest -> manage calories, thirst, fatigue, and warmth -> weather, night, and wildlife threaten condition -> craft, repair, and shelter -> survive another day until death
games.design_notes: Survival mode has no zombies or authored goal; the cold, wildlife, and dwindling supplies are the opposition, and death deletes the save. All needs feed a single condition stock: an empty warmth bar drains condition about 20% per hour while empty hunger or fatigue drain about 1% and thirst 2%, so cold is the fast killer and food is the slow one. Time is treated as the scarce resource because every action costs calories and in-game hours. The episodic Wintermute story mode has no permadeath.

mechanics.note: Warmth, fatigue, hunger, and thirst feed one condition stock; when a need is empty, condition drains per hour (warmth 20%, fatigue 1%, hunger 1%, thirst 2%), and afflictions such as hypothermia, frostbite, and dysentery drain or cap it.
Wind, falling temperatures, and blizzards change how fast warmth drops and how far the player can travel; nights are significantly colder.
In Survival mode the save is deleted on death; a later DLC option allows up to three resurrections per save at a difficulty cost, and Misery mode always uses permadeath.
Nights are darker and colder, shaping travel and shelter.
Hides, guts, and wood are crafted into clothing, tools, and arrows.
Clothing and tools lose condition with use and must be repaired.
Food loses condition over time.
Manufactured supplies are finite, so long runs shift from looting to hunting and crafting.

games.name: The Long Dark
games.summary: A first-person wilderness survival sim set in frozen northern Canada where the player manages warmth, calories, thirst, fatigue, and afflictions against cold, weather, and wildlife.

games.core_loop: paint elements onto the grid -> unpause the simulation -> watch particles fall, flow, burn, and react under pressure, heat, and electricity -> adjust or add elements -> save and share the build
games.design_notes: The Powder Toy combines a per-particle falling-sand layer with coarser fields for air pressure, air velocity, and heat, so explosions push air, air moves powders, and temperature thresholds change element states such as ice to water to steam. Electricity runs through conductive elements via sparks, and players build working logic gates, engines, and nuclear reactors from them. Element count passed 250 by 2025; the source is GPLv3 and the in-game save browser is the main distribution channel for builds.

mechanics.note: Each cell holds one particle of an element such as powder, liquid, gas, or solid, which moves by local rules each frame; element types numbered 258 as of February 2025.
Element pairs react by rule: acid dissolves most materials, acid and base neutralize into salt water, fuels ignite, and neutrons from radioactive elements can drive chain reactions.
Particles carry temperature that conducts to neighbors; melting and boiling thresholds change states, and the heat display shows the field.
A coarser grid of air pressure and velocity moves particles and is pushed by explosions and fans and blocked by walls.
Sparks conduct through metals and semiconductors to power switches, logic gates, and machines built from elements.
Fire and plasma ignite flammable elements and spread through fuel.
An online save browser with votes and comments distributes community builds.
A Lua API adds elements and automation scripts; the source is GPLv3 on GitHub.
The simulation can be paused and stepped frame by frame.

games.name: The Powder Toy
games.summary: An open-source falling-sand sandbox where hundreds of elements interact cell by cell under simulated air pressure, heat, gravity, and electricity.

games.core_loop: build and furnish the lot -> motives decay -> objects advertise motive gains and Sims act or take queued orders -> jobs pay for upgrades -> skills and friendships unlock promotions -> expand house and family
games.design_notes: Will Wright drew on Christopher Alexander's A Pattern Language, treating a house as a set of functional patterns judged by how well they serve the people living in it. Much of the behavioral logic sits in objects: each object advertises which motives it raises and by how much, and Sims with free will enabled choose among those advertisements weighted by their current motives. Sims are deliberately not fully autonomous, since paying bills, finding jobs, exercising, and having children need explicit commands, so the player alternates between architect and caretaker. Build and Buy modes pause time, separating spatial design from the live simulation.

mechanics.note: Eight motives (Hunger, Comfort, Hygiene, Bladder, Energy, Fun, Social, Room) decay at different rates; low motives drag down mood, and neglect can kill.
Each of the 150-plus base-game objects advertises motive gains (a refrigerator advertises Hunger, a bed Energy), and Sims query the lot's objects to find interactions.
Build and Buy modes freeze time while the player lays walls, floors, and objects on a square tile grid; object quality and layout set how efficiently motives can be met.
Free will scores advertised interactions against current motive levels so the most depleted motive tends to win; players can cancel queued autonomous actions.
Free will is an option toggle; even with it on, bills, job hunting, exercise, and having children need commands.
Twenty-five personality points are split across Neat, Outgoing, Active, Playful, and Nice, which change preferred activities and social outcomes.
Cooking, Mechanical, Charisma, Body, Logic, and Creativity rise through objects such as bookshelves, mirrors, and chess tables, and gate promotions.
Ten career tracks with ten levels each; promotions need skill points and a minimum number of household friends, and change salary and hours.
Every household starts with 20,000 simoleons regardless of size; wages, bills, and purchases set the balance.
Each pair holds a relationship score moved by interactions and eroding without contact; friend counts feed promotions.
Talk, joke, compliment, hug, kiss, tease, slap, and similar interactions succeed or fail on relationship, mood, and personality.
Sims can become partners, marry, and have a baby by explicit command; neglected babies can be taken away by a social worker.
The Room motive reflects lighting, cleanliness, and decorative value around the Sim.
Sims die from neglect or accidents and leave an urn or tombstone; the household continues without them.

games.name: The Sims
games.summary: A life sim in which the player builds a house and guides a household of Sims whose decaying motives, personalities, careers, and relationships produce an open-ended domestic story.

games.core_loop: create a household with aspirations -> wants and fears roll -> direct Sims to meet motives and wants -> aspiration meter and memories shift -> Sims age, marry, and have children who inherit genes -> continue with the next generation
games.design_notes: The Sims 2 turns the household sandbox into a generational one: babies become toddlers after 3 days, toddlers children after 4, children teens after 8, teens adults after 15, and adults elders after 29, and an elder's remaining life depends on the aspiration meter at the time of aging. Children inherit appearance and personality from both parents through dominant and recessive genes, and each Sim's aspiration (one of eight, such as Romance, Family, Knowledge, or Popularity) biases which wants and fears appear. The wants-and-fears panel is a short-horizon goal generator with no mechanic id yet (proposed as aspiration-wants). SimPE and Body Shop made behavior hacks and custom genetics routine in its mod community.

mechanics.note: Eight motives (Hunger, Comfort, Bladder, Energy, Fun, Social, Hygiene, Environment) decay and push Sims toward objects; failing motives cause refusals and, at the extreme, death.
Objects advertise motive and skill gains that autonomous Sims weigh against their current motive levels.
Seven life stages (baby, toddler, child, teen, young adult with University, adult, elder) advance on fixed day counts; a birthday cake or Grow Up interaction ages a Sim early.
Children inherit eye color, hair color, facial structure, and personality from both parents through dominant and recessive genes; pregnancy lasts 3 Sim days.
Events such as a first kiss, a promotion, or a death are stored as memories that later shape wants and fears.
Twenty-five points are spread over five opposed pairs (Neat/Sloppy, Outgoing/Shy, Active/Lazy, Playful/Serious, Nice/Grouchy); twelve zodiac presets give starting allocations.
Careers have ten levels (25 tracks counting expansions); promotions need skills and a number of family friends, and chance cards can reward or cost the job.
Each pair holds a daily and a lifetime relationship score that move with interactions.
Sims court, marry, and try for babies; Nightlife adds turn-ons and turn-offs shown as up to three chemistry bolts.
Build and Buy modes in a free 3D camera; neighborhood terrain can be imported from SimCity 4.
Elders die of old age and other Sims of accidents or neglect; deaths become memories for survivors.

Each Sim's aspiration (one of eight, such as Romance, Family, Knowledge, or Popularity) biases which wants and fears roll; fulfilled wants fill the aspiration meter, realized fears drain it, and an elder's remaining life depends on the meter.

games.name: The Sims 2
games.summary: The 3D sequel to The Sims that adds aging through seven life stages, genetic inheritance, aspirations with wants and fears, and memories, so households play across generations.

games.core_loop: pick traits and a lifetime wish -> moodlets from events stack into mood -> wishes and opportunities appear -> act across the open town -> earn Lifetime Happiness for rewards -> story progression advances other households
games.design_notes: Neighborhoods are seamless worlds, so Sims walk between lots without loading screens on PC, and Story Progression keeps households the player is not controlling aging, working, and forming relationships. Personality is a set of up to five discrete traits that unlock and bias interactions, and mood is the sum of moodlets, timed modifiers with named causes. Fulfilled wishes pay Lifetime Happiness points spent on Lifetime Rewards, replacing the wants and fears of The Sims 2. Off-screen story progression and wish generation are captured by the offscreen-life-progression and aspiration-wants mechanics.

mechanics.note: Adult Sims hold up to five traits chosen from a list, replacing the point sliders of earlier games; traits add exclusive interactions and bias autonomous choices.
Moodlets are named, timed mood modifiers (for example Nauseous during pregnancy) whose sum sets mood, which affects performance at work and school.
Six motives (Hunger, Bladder, Energy, Social, Hygiene, Fun) decay and spawn negative moodlets when low.
Objects advertise motive, skill, and fun gains; traits bias which advertisements a Sim picks.
Opportunities arrive from neighbors, community lots, and jobs, such as skill requests or overtime, and pay cash, raises, or relationship gains.
Twelve base careers that branch around level 6, plus part-time jobs; a performance style (Work Hard, Take It Easy, Suck Up to Boss) trades mood against promotion speed.
Ten-level skills such as Logic, Cooking, Painting, Gardening, Writing, Guitar, Athletic, Handiness, Charisma, and Fishing feed careers and opportunities.
Seven life stages with an adjustable lifespan setting.
Conversation menus offer trait- and mood-gated interactions whose acceptance depends on relationship state.
Jobs and school run on fixed hours at rabbit-hole buildings, structuring each household's day.
Build and Buy modes with Create-a-Style, which recolors walls, floors, objects, and clothing with any pattern and material.
Sims die of old age or of fire, starvation, drowning, or electrocution.
A Lifetime Wish is chosen at creation and short-term wishes appear from traits and events; fulfilled wishes pay Lifetime Happiness points spent on Lifetime Rewards.
Story Progression keeps households the player is not controlling aging, working, forming relationships, and moving around the open neighborhood; it can be switched off in the options.

games.name: The Sims 3
games.summary: The third mainline Sims game, which places households in a seamless open neighborhood where unplayed Sims keep living, and replaces personality sliders with up to five traits and mood with stacked moodlets.

games.core_loop: build a home or download one from the Gallery -> moodlets from events and surroundings set the dominant emotion -> emotion unlocks interactions and speeds skills -> pursue aspiration milestones and a career -> earn rewards -> share households and builds
games.design_notes: The Sims 4 makes emotion the central state: moodlets from actions, events, objects, and social interactions carry an emotion type and weight, and the strongest set the Sim's single dominant emotion, which gates emotional interactions and speeds matching skills. Adult personality is three traits plus a bonus trait from the chosen aspiration, and completing aspiration milestones grants reward traits. Build mode treats rooms as units that can be moved, duplicated, saved to a library, and shared through the Gallery; the base game became free to play on 2022-10-18. Neighborhood Stories, a free update that advances unplayed households, is the offscreen-life-progression mechanic.

mechanics.note: Moodlets carry an emotion type (such as Happy, Focused, Flirty, Angry, Tense, or Sad), an intensity, and a timer; the highest-weighted emotion becomes the Sim's dominant emotion.
Adults hold three traits and children and teens two, plus one bonus trait from the aspiration; traits add moodlets, autonomous behaviors, and exclusive interactions.
Six needs (Hunger, Bladder, Energy, Social, Hygiene, Fun) decay and spawn negative moodlets such as Hungry or Bored when low.

Dominant emotions unlock emotion-specific interactions and raise gain for matching skills (Inspired for creative, Focused for mental, Energized for physical); extreme states such as Hysterical can kill.
Objects advertise need, skill, and emotion gains, and Sims multitask, such as talking while cooking.
Build mode draws walls and rooms, places premade rooms, and moves or duplicates whole rooms.
Sims, households, rooms, and lots can be saved to a personal library and placed again.
The Gallery uploads and downloads Sims, households, rooms, and buildings from other players inside the game.
Newborn, infant, toddler, child, teen, young adult, adult, and elder; toddlers were added in 2017 and newborn and infant in 2023.
Careers require related skills, for example Cooking and Mixology for Culinary.
Separate friendship and romance bars per pair.
Social menus are filtered by emotion and traits, with emotion-specific variants of interactions.
Free will can be toggled; with it off Sims act only on player orders except for urgent needs.
The chosen aspiration grants a bonus trait and a track of milestones whose completion earns reward traits; short-term whims, later reworked as wants and fears, appear from emotions and traits.

Neighborhood Stories, added in a free update, advances unplayed households with events such as moves, relationships, and births, with settings that limit which households and event types it may touch.

games.name: The Sims 4
games.summary: The fourth mainline Sims game, built around a dominant emotion computed from moodlets, three-trait personalities with aspiration rewards, multitasking, room-based building, and an in-game Gallery for sharing creations.

games.core_loop: build rooms from blueprints -> hire and train staff -> patients queue for GP diagnosis and referrals -> treatment cures or kills -> fees and reputation -> research new rooms and meet level goals
games.design_notes: Theme Hospital turns medicine into routing. The GP and specialist diagnosis rooms raise a patient's diagnosis certainty, and the player sets the threshold at which treatment starts (it can be set above 100%), trading throughput against deaths from wrong cures. Rooms are fixed blueprints that need set furniture and, for some, specialist staff, so the staff roster and the floor plan gate each other. Machines that explode without a handyman, epidemics that can be covered up before the health inspector arrives, and timed emergencies add pressure on top of the queues. Much of the code came from Theme Park; CorsixTH is an open-source reimplementation with a level editor.

mechanics.note: A GP diagnoses or refers patients to specialist diagnosis rooms; treatment starts once certainty passes a player-set threshold, and diseases are fictional, such as Bloaty Head.
Rooms are placed as blueprints with doors and windows, then furnished with required items; many rooms must be researched first.
Doctors, nurses, handymen, and receptionists are hired with performance stats; some rooms need doctors with specialist skills.
Patients queue outside each room; the player can rearrange queues, and long waits push patients to leave.
Doctors can be trained to gain skills and specialisms.
Machines such as the Inflator need handyman servicing or they explode.
Epidemics break out and can be covered up before a health inspector visits; failure brings fines and lost reputation.
Research unlocks rooms, drugs, and machine improvements.
Cures and deaths move a reputation that affects patient intake and level goals.
Staff tire and need breaks under player-set break rules; patients need drinks and toilets.
Emergencies require curing a group of patients within a time limit for a bonus.
Each level sets goals for money, reputation, cures, and hospital value; negative funds or too many deaths lose the level.

games.name: Theme Hospital
games.summary: A hospital management game where the player builds rooms, hires and trains staff, and routes patients with comic diseases through diagnosis and treatment to meet level goals.

games.core_loop: place rides, shops, and paths -> visitors arrive by bus and choose attractions -> tune prices and shop ingredients -> fund research and hire staff -> yearly judging against rivals -> sell the park and buy a plot abroad
games.design_notes: Theme Park gives every visitor its own record (about 200 bytes each) and lets the player change the product as well as its price: ingredient settings such as sugar in ice cream trade cost against whether customers return. The full-simulation level adds wage and supply negotiations, where failure means staff strikes or lost shipments, plus research funding and shares; the sandbox level removes them, so one engine serves three depths. Unhappy visitors attract thugs, which ties satisfaction to crime. Negotiation has no mechanic in the taxonomy (proposed as negotiation).

mechanics.note: Each visitor is an individual with its own personality and arrives and leaves by bus; unhappy crowds draw thugs who vandalize and attack entertainers.
Entry, ride, and shop prices plus ingredient levels such as sugar in ice cream decide what visitors buy and whether they come back.
Over thirty attractions, shops, toilets, and scenery are placed on a plot, with coasters needing laid-out track.
Rides wear down and explode if mechanics do not maintain them; research can make rides more durable.
Entertainers, security guards, mechanics, and handymen are hired and their wages negotiated; understaffing brings litter, breakdowns, and crime.
Visitors need food, drink, and toilets as their visit goes on.
Visitors queue for rides and shops.
A funding level drives research into new items, ride durability, staff efficiency, and bus capacity.
Thugs appear when visitors are unhappy; security guards counter them.
The park is judged against rival parks each year.
On the full-simulation level, staff wage talks and supply negotiations are haggles; failed wage talks end in strikes and failed supply talks in lost shipments.

games.name: Theme Park
games.summary: A theme park management game in which the player builds rides and shops, tunes prices and recipes for individually simulated visitors, and sells parks to expand worldwide.

games.core_loop: spend the day in the shelter crafting, cooking, trading, and treating -> assign night roles -> one survivor scavenges a location -> encounters force moral choices -> hunger, wounds, illness, and mood shift -> survive until the ceasefire
games.design_notes: The game turns war into a resource-and-conscience problem: survival needs push the player toward theft or violence, and those acts lower survivors' mood, so material and moral states are coupled. A day-night split separates base management (snipers keep survivors inside by day) from risky scavenging by one chosen survivor, and the length of the war is randomized so the player cannot plan to a known end. The radio reports weather, prices, and war news that let the player anticipate shortages. It draws on the 1992-96 Siege of Sarajevo.

mechanics.note: Snipers confine survivors to the shelter by day for crafting, cooking, and care; at night survivors are assigned to sleep, guard, or scavenge.
Each survivor tracks hunger, fatigue, health, and mood, and the player must keep them up until the ceasefire.

Mood falls with hunger, illness, loss of companions, and morally weighted acts such as stealing or killing; depressed or broken survivors refuse tasks and may leave the shelter or take their own lives.
Scavenging encounters and visitors at the door pose choices, such as robbing vulnerable NPCs or giving away supplies, that trade material gain against mood and each survivor's ending.
Each survivor has one or two traits, such as Good Cook, plus hidden stats.
Workshops craft weapons, alcohol, beds, stoves, and shelter upgrades from scavenged materials.
Radio broadcasts give weather warnings, economic updates, and war news.
Barter values change with conditions announced on the radio.
Winter raises demand for heating fuel.
Neighbors and strangers arrive with requests tied to the shelter's state.
Noisy actions while scavenging at night, such as breaking through obstacles, can alert people at the location.

games.name: This War of Mine
games.summary: A survival sim about civilians in a besieged city who maintain a shelter by day, scavenge by night, and face moral choices that change their mood until a randomized ceasefire.

games.core_loop: dam and channel rivers -> irrigate farms and forests from stored water -> beavers work, eat, and seek wellbeing -> a drought or badtide cuts or poisons the flow -> stockpiles and reservoirs carry the colony through -> build upward and expand
games.design_notes: Water is a simulated field rather than a resource count: a 2D model adapted from erosion simulation linked each tile to four neighbors by virtual pipes and was replaced by 3D water in Update 6 (October 2024), so dams, floodgates, and canals change where moisture reaches crops. Recurring droughts grow harsher and badtides turn sources into contaminating badwater, so play alternates between building reservoirs and surviving a known dry period. Limited space pushes housing and workshops into vertical stacks, and sensors and relays let players automate floodgates.

mechanics.note: Tiles exchange water through virtual pipes with evaporation; moisture spreads to nearby land and falls off sharply uphill; dams, levees, floodgates, and canals redirect flow.
Recurring droughts switch sources off and badtides release contaminating badwater; both grow harsher over time and are signalled in advance.
Explosives dig tunnels and reshape terrain.
Lodges and workshops stack on platforms; ziplines and tubeways move beavers between levels.
Crops grow only on irrigated soil and fail when it dries.
Beavers need food, water, rest, and wellbeing from diet variety, entertainment, and decorations.
