Skill abstraction from one demonstration often over- or under-generalizes.
Runtime cost of a capable agent on consumer hardware.
opportunities.name: Teachable sim companion
opportunities.summary: A co-player agent that learns factory, colony, or farm routines from demonstration and language, and grows a library of reusable skills the player can inspect.
opportunities.thesis: Generalist game agents (SIMA, SIMA 2) follow language instructions across 3D games, and Voyager showed skill libraries of reusable code that grow over play. Automation games already reward teaching: Autonauts made programming bots by demonstration the core loop. A companion that learns skills from the player and stores them as inspectable, shareable routines turns automation from wiring to mentoring.
opportunities.validation_experiment: In a voxel automation prototype, have players teach five routines by demonstration and narration; measure how often the learned skill succeeds in a new location and whether players report more or less enjoyment than blueprints. Success: 70 percent transfer success and preference over blueprints for at least half of players.

opportunities.design_sketch: The player raises a creature in a small world. Rewards, punishments, demonstrations, and spoken commands shape its policy. A 'what I learned' panel lists the creature's inferred rules in plain language with examples; the player can correct misunderstandings. Creatures can be traded and bred, inheriting learned dispositions partially.

falsifiable_signal.criteria: Developer documentation describing on-device or server learning of a creature policy from player feedback.
falsifiable_signal.prediction: A commercial virtual-pet or god game will ship a creature whose behavior is trained online by player feedback with a learned model.

key_risks: Learning that is too slow or too fast reads as fake.
Reward hacking produces creatures that game the player.
On-device training cost.
opportunities.name: Trainable creatures revival
opportunities.summary: Revive the Creatures and Black & White lineage with creatures whose behavior is genuinely learned from player feedback and can explain itself.
opportunities.thesis: Creatures (1996) used neural networks and genetics; Black & White (2001) let a creature learn from slaps and strokes. Both were limited by tiny learning systems that generalized poorly and were opaque. Modern reinforcement learning, preference learning, and small language models allow a creature that learns real policies from feedback, generalizes to new situations, and can say in simple words what it thinks it was rewarded for.
opportunities.validation_experiment: Build a creature with a learned policy trained online from player feedback in a 2D world; measure how many feedback events it takes to learn three behaviors and whether its self-explanations match its actual policy. Success: under 30 feedback events per behavior and 80 percent explanation accuracy.

opportunities.design_sketch: Solar and wind output follow simulated weather; heating and cooling demand follow temperature; the player builds storage, buys forecasts, and sets demand-response policies. Rare long calm, cold spells test the grid. Prices respond to scarcity if the game has markets.

falsifiable_signal.criteria: Developer documentation describing weather-dependent renewable output and storage in the grid system.
falsifiable_signal.prediction: A commercial city builder or management game will couple renewable generation to simulated weather as a core grid mechanic.

key_risks: Realistic intermittency may frustrate players without good forecasting tools.
Weather that dominates the economy reduces player agency.
opportunities.name: Weather-coupled energy grids
opportunities.summary: Power grids whose renewable supply follows realistic weather, so storage, forecasting, and demand response become the grid puzzle.
opportunities.thesis: Power grids and weather are both common in the catalog but almost never coupled; most games treat generation as constant. Learned weather emulators make realistic, correlated wind, sun, and temperature affordable, and the coupling creates a familiar modern problem: balancing intermittent supply with storage, forecasts, and flexible demand.
opportunities.validation_experiment: Couple a city prototype's grid to a weather emulator and test whether players with forecast tools build mixed storage strategies rather than one dominant plant type. Success: strategy diversity increases and blackout frustration ratings stay below the baseline game's disaster ratings.

sources.name: MudRunner: Porting a Successful Title to Console
sources.notes: Interview with Pavel Zagrebelny (lead developer, Spintires: MudRunner) and Saber staff: terrain is a regular vertex grid displaced by a height map with an artist-painted mud layer and a higher-resolution mud grid; mud forces computed when wheels are in mud or spin fast; mud displacement runs on the GPU.

sources.name: Noita: a Game Based on Falling Sand Simulation
sources.notes: Interview with Petri Purho: liquids fall then spread and swap by density; gases rise; fire ignites random neighbors; wood burns then disappears; 64x64 chunks with dirty rects; bottom-up updates in four checkerboard passes; pixels may move 32 px beyond their chunk; pixel rigid bodies split as pixels are destroyed.

sources.name: See What's New In Teardown Creator's Custom Voxel Physics Engine
sources.notes: Dennis Gustafsson's new engine uses substepping instead of solver iterations (temporal Gauss-Seidel), a parallel solver for large piles, improved contacts and broad phase; about 5 ms simulation on a 32-thread CPU; credits Erin Catto's Box2D work.

sources.name: Simulation Principles from Dwarf Fortress
sources.notes: World generation begins with a randomized fractal elevation map, then temperature, rainfall, drainage, vegetation, and salinity layers, then land classification. Principles: do not overplan, break down the system, do not overcomplicate, base models on real-world analogs.
sources.venue: Game AI Pro 2, ed. Steve Rabin, CRC Press (chapter 41)

sources.name: Using Large Language Models to Simulate Multiple Humans and Replicate Human Subject Studies
sources.notes: Turing Experiments: models replicated Ultimatum Game, garden path sentence, and Milgram shock findings; a wisdom-of-crowds experiment revealed a hyper-accuracy distortion in ChatGPT and GPT-4.

sources.name: Skillful joint probabilistic weather forecasting from marginals
sources.notes: FGN: ensembles from learned model perturbations trained on per-location CRPS; state-of-the-art ensemble skill and cyclone tracks while capturing joint spatial structure.

sources.name: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Navigation in AAA Video Games
sources.notes: Ubisoft La Forge; learned navigation for grappling hooks, jetpacks, teleporters, and double jumps on maps about ten times larger than typical RL maps, one modeled on a Ubisoft AAA game; at least 90% success.

sources.name: Diffusion for World Modeling: Visual Details Matter in Atari
sources.notes: DIAMOND: Atari 100k mean HNS 1.46. CS:GO world model from 87 h of human play, about 10 fps on an RTX 3090, trained 12 days on an RTX 4090; allows repeated jumps the real game forbids.

sources.name: Project Sid: Many-agent simulations toward AI civilization
sources.notes: PIANO architecture with concurrent modules and a cognitive controller; 10 to 1000+ agents in Minecraft (results up to 500); role specialization; 29-agent constitution and 20 percent tax experiment with influencers and votes; Pastafarianism seeded by 20 priests; GPT-4o base model.

sources.name: Deep Dive: Designing the dynamic irrigation and water systems in Timberborn
sources.notes: Single-layer 2D water model adapted from erosion simulation; tiles linked to four neighbors by virtual pipes; ticks every couple of hundred ms; water levels equalize; evaporation; recurring droughts grow harsher and ramp source strength down early; hard-coded dam values avoided because they caused oscillations; moisture falls off per tile and sharply uphill.

sources.name: Needs
sources.notes: Basic needs raise inhabitants per house; luxury needs raise taxes and happiness; houses must be full to advance tiers; consumption measured per residence per second.

sources.name: Population
sources.notes: Old World tiers Farmers, Workers, Artisans, Engineers, Investors; New World Jornaleros and Obreros; a house advances when full, basic needs are met, and construction materials are available; luxury needs are optional and raise taxes and happiness; island level set by the highest tier, such as 500 Engineers (capital) and 1,750 Investors (metropolis).

sources.name: Mindustry source repository
sources.notes: README describes 'The automation tower defense RTS, written in Java'; GPL-3.0; desktop, Android, and server builds.

sources.name: Out of One, Many: Using Language Models to Simulate Human Samples
sources.notes: Silicon samples: GPT-3 conditioned on thousands of sociodemographic backstories from U.S. survey participants reproduces subgroup response distributions; the property is named algorithmic fidelity.

sources.name: V-JEPA 2: Self-Supervised Video Models Enable Understanding, Prediction and Planning
sources.notes: Over 1M hours of video and images; V-JEPA 2-AC post-trained on under 62 h of DROID robot video; zero-shot pick-and-place with image goals on Franka arms in two labs; SSv2 77.3, EK-100 R@5 39.7.

sources.name: Bots
sources.notes: Bots combine a head, body, and drive from Mk 0 to Mk 3; head sets max instructions (12 to 32) and find range; body sets hand, backpack, and upgrade slots; drive sets speed, recharge time, and battery; upgrades include brain, sensor, speed, and energy.

sources.name: Folk
sources.notes: Folk need housing, food (satiation from 10 s for water to 120 s for apple pie or cooked fish), and cleaning such as baths after messy meals; each folk is fully happy or unhappy; no clothing need as of version 21.2.

sources.name: Introduction to JBeam
sources.notes: Soft-body vehicles as nodes (point masses) and beams (massless springs that do not resist bending or torsion); beamSpring, beamDamp, beamDeform, beamStrength; cross braces required for rigidity; stiff beams on light nodes vibrate or explode (6 kg vs 7 kg node example); typical values such as suspension spring 40000.

sources.name: Augmenting Automated Game Testing with Deep Reinforcement Learning
sources.notes: EA SEED; four sandbox environments; an RL agent found a wall missing its collision mesh that scripted navmesh agents missed, and timeouts located all five stuck areas.

sources.name: Deep Surrogate Assisted Generation of Environments
A foundation model to predict and capture human cognition
sources.notes: Centaur: Llama 3.1 70B, frozen 4-bit base, rank-8 QLoRA adapters (about 0.15% of parameters), one epoch, about five days on one A100 80GB. Psych-101: 160 experiments, 60,092 participants, 10,681,650 choices. Beats 14 cognitive models on held-out participants; generalizes to new cover stories, structures, domains. Limits: WEIRD bias, mostly learning and decision tasks, 8B Minitaur weaker out of distribution.

sources.name: Bitburner changelog (v0)
sources.notes: Pre-1.0 changelog; versions from v0.15.0 are undated, and the earliest dated entry is v0.26.4 on 2017-08-01.

sources.name: Bitburner changelog (v1)
sources.notes: Version 1.0.0 is dated 2021-11-10.

sources.name: Blackshark.ai
sources.notes: HUNTR and REPLIKA products turn satellite and aerial imagery into structured digital models of terrain, buildings, and infrastructure; Zurich showcase.

sources.name: A foundation model for the Earth system
sources.notes: Aurora, 1.3B parameters, pretrained on over one million hours of geophysical data; fine-tuned for air quality, ocean waves, cyclone tracks, 0.1 degree weather; about 100,000x faster than CAMS for air quality.

sources.name: sbi reloaded: a toolkit for simulation-based inference workflows
sources.notes: PyTorch sbi package: neural posterior, likelihood and ratio estimators, diagnostics, amortized inference; needs only simulator samples, no gradients.

sources.name: The AI Systems of Left 4 Dead
sources.notes: Slides hosted by Valve; venue from the AAAI AIIDE 2009 speaker list. AI Director adaptive pacing: per-survivor emotional intensity rises with damage, incapacitation, and nearby kills and decays when not engaged; phases Build Up, Sustain Peak (3-5 s), Peak Fade, Relax (30-45 s); mobs every 90-180 s on Normal; boss events (Tank, Witch, nothing) shuffled along the route.
sources.venue: Artificial Intelligence and Interactive Digital Entertainment Conference (AIIDE) 2009, Stanford

sources.name: Wave Function Collapse Explained
sources.notes: WFC as constraint programming based on Paul Merrell's model synthesis; contradictions; local constraints rarely give large-scale structure; overlapping model slower and can copy the sample.

sources.name: Superhuman AI for heads-up no-limit poker: Libratus beats top professionals
Superhuman AI for multiplayer poker
sources.notes: Pluribus beat professionals in six-player no-limit hold'em with a self-play blueprint plus real-time search.

sources.name: Combining Deep Reinforcement Learning and Search for Imperfect-Information Games
sources.notes: ReBeL: self-play RL plus search that provably converges to a Nash equilibrium in two-player zero-sum games; reduces to an AlphaZero-like algorithm in perfect-information games; superhuman heads-up no-limit hold'em.

sources.name: Evolutionary Game Design
sources.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Intelligence and AI in Games 2(1):1-16

sources.name: A Survey of Monte Carlo Tree Search Methods
sources.notes: Survey of MCTS variants, enhancements, and game and non-game applications after its first years.
sources.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Intelligence and AI in Games 4(1):1-43

sources.name: Genie: Generative Interactive Environments
sources.notes: 11B foundation world model from unlabeled video; 30k h of 2D platformer clips (6.8M 16 s clips); 8 latent actions; tokenizer ~200M, LAM ~300M, dynamics 10.1B; ~1 fps; 16-frame memory.

sources.name: Space Haven
sources.notes: Official page: spaceship colony sim inspired by RimWorld, Dwarf Fortress, Spacebase DF-9, and Oxygen Not Included, combining RimWorld-style emergent stories with a tile-based gas simulation.

sources.name: PANGeA: Procedural Artificial Narrative using Generative AI for Turn-Based Video Games
sources.notes: LLM generates settings, key items, and NPCs from designer criteria for turn-based RPGs; Big Five personality-biased NPCs; LLM validates free-text player input against the narrative; memory server with REST interface for any engine; tested in a custom GPT and a Unity demo.

sources.name: Julius: an open source re-implementation of Caesar III
sources.notes: Aims for exactly the same game logic as Caesar III. Read src/figure/movement.c (roaming), src/figure/service.c (MAX_COVERAGE 96; prefect zeroes fire risk; engineer zeroes damage risk), src/building/house_service.c (coverage decays by 1).

sources.name: Little Computer People
sources.notes: Community wiki; publication date not stated, accessed revision. Keyboard care commands (food, water, pat, gifts), sickness from not eating, mood faces, polite typed requests, per-disk serial seed for name, personality, and behavior.

sources.name: Applications of Mean Field Games in Financial Engineering and Economic Theory
sources.notes: Review of MFG applications in finance and economics, including bitcoin mining, energy markets, macro-finance models and contract theory.

sources.name: Lenia: Biology of Artificial Life
sources.notes: Continuous space-time-state cellular automaton with a ring kernel and growth function; over 400 species in 18 families, many found by interactive evolutionary search.

sources.name: Differentiable Agent-based Epidemiology
sources.notes: GradABM: tensorized differentiable agent-based epidemic model; million-agent populations in a few seconds on commodity hardware; gradient-based calibration to COVID-19 and influenza data.

sources.name: GDC 2012: Breaking down SimCity's Glassbox engine
sources.notes: Reports Andrew Willmott's GDC 2012 talk: units hold resource bins with capacities (a house with 20/30 food, 4/10 people); rules move or combine resources; agents carry resources, including units of water in pipes; maps hold depletable resources.

sources.name: Dumping Designation
sources.notes: Mining designations must lie within a Mine Control Tower area; trucks unload into dumping designations; retaining walls stabilize terrain; materials have densities and angles of repose from about 42 degrees for loose dirt and sand to 78 degrees for hardened rock.

sources.name: Maintenance
sources.notes: Maintenance I-III is crafted at depots and consumed by working vehicles and buildings (idle at about a third); below 75% a breakdown becomes possible, rising to 50% at 0, checked monthly; Unity can repair a single unit.

sources.name: Population
sources.notes: Natural growth depends on colony health; population falls 0.1% per month per health point below 0; diseases and radiation cause further losses; villages can be adopted for Unity.

sources.name: Unity
sources.notes: Each fully satisfied settlement need yields about 1-2 Unity per month; Unity is spent on edicts, outposts, quick trades, contracts, research lab I, quick-build, vehicle recovery, emergency repairs, and building boosts (0.25 each).

sources.name: Road to the IGF: Zachtronics' Opus Magnum
sources.notes: Interview with Zach Barth and Matthew Burns: metrics are cost, area, and cycles; friends' scores motivate optimization; the team deliberately offers no in-game rewards for optimization.

sources.name: The frontier of simulation-based inference
sources.notes: Review of likelihood-free inference for simulators with intractable likelihoods, including neural posterior, likelihood and ratio estimation.

sources.name: Bitburner (original repository)
sources.notes: Original repository by danielyxie describing 'a programming-based incremental game that revolves around hacking and cyberpunk themes'; playable in the browser and on Steam; development moved to bitburner-official/bitburner-src.

sources.name: Oasis project page (Decart and Etched)
sources.notes: Real-time Minecraft-like world model at 20 fps; ViT spatial autoencoder plus latent DiT; Diffusion Forcing and dynamic noising; 500M open weights plus hosted larger model; limitations: fuzzy distance, weak memory (~3 s example), imprecise inventory, weak domain generalization.

sources.name: MirageLSD: live-stream diffusion video model
sources.notes: Live video-to-video diffusion with text prompts; under 40 ms response, 24 fps; Diffusion Forcing, history augmentation, Hopper kernels, pruning, shortcut distillation; limitations: limited past-frame window, weak object and region control, distortion under extreme style shifts.

sources.name: How to Play Oasis 2.0
sources.notes: Minecraft 1.21.8 mod using Decart's V2V model to transform the world in real time; /oasis start, /oasis prompt, key bindings to cycle prompts and toggle the stream; command blocks issue Oasis$prompt, show, hide, toggle.

sources.name: MuZero's first step from research into the real world
sources.notes: MuZero-RC chose VP9 quantisation parameters per frame on part of YouTube live traffic; average 4% bitrate reduction without quality loss; objective framed as win/loss against the agent's own past performance.

sources.name: GraphCast: AI model for faster and more accurate global weather forecasting
sources.notes: 10-day forecast in under a minute on one TPU v4 machine versus hours for HRES on a supercomputer; beat HRES on over 90% of 1,380 targets; code released.

sources.name: Genie 2: A large-scale foundation world model
sources.notes: Image prompt to playable 3D world; consistent up to a minute, most examples 10-20 s; re-renders off-screen parts; water, smoke, gravity, lighting; NPCs; autoregressive latent diffusion; SIMA agent tests; prototyping from concept art.

sources.name: A generalist AI agent for 3D virtual environments
sources.notes: 600 basic skills; nine commercial games (Valheim, Teardown, No Man's Sky, Wobbly Life, Satisfactory, Goat Simulator 3, Hydroneer, Space Engineers, Eco) plus four research environments. Generalist outperformed per-game specialists; held-out-game agent nearly matched specialist. Tasks about 10 seconds; no multi-step strategic planning.

sources.name: Scaling Instructable Agents Across Many Simulated Worlds
sources.notes: Agents take image observations and language instructions and output keyboard and mouse actions through a generic human-like interface in real time, across research environments and commercial games.

sources.name: AlphaEvolve: A Gemini-powered coding agent for designing advanced algorithms
sources.notes: Borg scheduling heuristic recovers about 0.7% of Google fleet compute; 4x4 complex matrix multiply in 48 multiplications; over 50 open problems: ~75% matched, ~20% improved; Gemini kernel 23% faster.

sources.name: Genie 3: A new frontier for world models
sources.notes: 720p, 24 fps real time; consistent for a few minutes; visual memory about one minute; promptable world events (weather, objects, characters); limits: action space, multi-agent interaction, geographic accuracy, text, duration; limited research preview.

sources.name: SIMA 2: An Agent that Plays, Reasons, and Learns With You in Virtual 3D Worlds
sources.notes: Gemini core; reasons about goals, explains actions, converses, answers questions about environment; follows sketches, emoji, multiple languages; unseen games ASKA and MineDojo and Genie 3 worlds; self-improvement from Gemini-proposed tasks and rewards. Limited research preview for academics and developers.

sources.name: SIMA 2: A Generalist Embodied Agent for Virtual Worlds
sources.notes: Roughly doubles SIMA 1 average success, approaching humans; over 10% better than SIMA 1 on held-out ASKA and MineDojo; 26 of 50 MineDojo categories. Task setter plus reward model scoring 0-100 (>=50 success). Gemini Flash-Lite base for latency; SFT cut AIME about 25.5%; weak combat; short memory.

sources.name: Concordia: a library for generative social simulation
sources.notes: Apache-2.0. Entities (player agents and Game Masters), components, and an engine loop. LanguageModel interface defines sample_text and sample_choice; sample_choice scores a list of candidate responses and returns the chosen index, raising InvalidResponseError after several failed attempts. Requires a text embedder for associative memory.

sources.name: MuJoCo Warp (MJWarp)
sources.notes: GPU MuJoCo on NVIDIA Warp, maintained within the Newton project; batch renderer for many cameras across worlds; some solvers unsupported; differentiability via Warp not yet available.

sources.name: Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue
sources.notes: Full-duplex spoken dialogue as speech-to-speech generation from a text LM backbone; models user and system speech as parallel codec token streams; Inner Monologue predicts time-aligned text before audio. Latency 160 ms theoretical, 200 ms practical.

sources.name: Autonauts
sources.notes: Price-tracking listing aggregating console stores: Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One versions released 2022-06-16.

sources.name: Historical figure
sources.notes: Only part of each site's population becomes historical figures (nobles and entourage, megabeasts, villains, their families); the world total is capped in advanced world generation with optional culling; figures track family, titles, kills, and relationships.

sources.name: Legends
sources.notes: Legends mode lists historical figures, sites, artifacts, written works, regions, civilizations, and Chronicles by Age; player achievements are recorded; Reveal All Historical Events option; XML export can reach about a gigabyte for long histories.

sources.name: Stress
sources.notes: Hidden stress value from -1,000,000 to +1,000,000 with effects at +10,000, +25,000, and +50,000; emotions add or subtract stress; facets such as bravery, stress vulnerability, and anxiety scale it; short-term and long-term memories; tantrums, depression, obliviousness, Harrowed, insanity.

sources.name: Improving AI Decision Modeling Through Utility Theory
sources.notes: Argues that if-then logic makes agent decisions switch abruptly; proposes utility theory with response curves, population distributions, and weighted random selection for more natural decisions, wider action ranges, and better edge-case handling.

sources.name: XGrammar: Flexible and Efficient Structured Generation Engine for Large Language Models
sources.notes: CFG-constrained decoding; vocabulary split into context-independent tokens prechecked and context-dependent tokens checked at runtime with a persistent stack; grammar work overlapped with GPU execution; up to 100x faster than prior solutions, near-zero end-to-end overhead.

sources.name: Day-Night Cycle
sources.notes: Default day lasts 8 real minutes in sixteen 30-second segments of day, dusk, and night; split varies by season; base cycle 36 days (20 summer, 16 winter); Charlie attacks in total darkness; sanity drain 5/min at dusk, 50/min in total darkness at night, 5/min near light.

sources.name: Hound
sources.notes: Default hound attack schedule: days 1-10 every 5-8 days with 2 hounds and 120 s warning, rising to days 101+ every 11-16 days with 7-10 hounds and 30 s warning; red and blue hound chances rise with days survived.

sources.name: Hunger
sources.notes: Default maximum hunger 150; drains 9.375 per minute (75 per game day); at empty hunger health drains 1.25 per second until the character eats or dies; cooked food usually restores more than raw.

sources.name: Dark Fog
sources.notes: Space hives and planetary bases built around relays; threat builds from the player's power generation and from combat; bases and hives gain levels from experience; aggressiveness and growth settings; relays rebuild a destroyed hive core.

sources.name: Dyson Sphere
sources.notes: Solar sails fired by EM-Rail Ejectors give 36 kW base scaled by star luminosity and last 5,400 s by default; Small Carrier Rockets from Vertical Launching Silos build frames; completed shells absorb swarm sails permanently; Ray Receivers start at 30% efficiency and can make critical photons.

sources.name: Interstellar Logistics Station
sources.notes: Per-item local and remote storage, supply, and demand settings; up to 100 logistics drones and 10 logistics vessels per station; vessels warp between stars after Logistics Carrier Engine level 4 using Space Warpers; pairing priority is point-to-point, then interstellar routes, then groups.

sources.name: Calibrating Agent-based Models to Microdata with Graph Neural Networks
sources.notes: Temporal graph neural networks learn ABM parameter posteriors directly from agent-level microstates instead of hand-chosen summary statistics.

sources.name: Black-box Bayesian inference for economic agent-based models
sources.notes: Neural posterior estimation and neural ratio estimation give state-of-the-art parameter inference for economic ABMs from multivariate time series, versus older methods needing hundreds of thousands of runs.
sources.venue: Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control

sources.name: Illuminating Diverse Neural Cellular Automata for Level Generation
sources.notes: CMA-ME quality-diversity search over NCA generators for maze, Sokoban and Zelda levels; NCAs explore level space better than a CPPN baseline.

sources.name: ECMWF's AI forecasts become operational
sources.notes: AIFS Single made operational alongside IFS; about 1,000x less energy per forecast; 28 km grid versus 9 km for IFS; ensemble version planned.

sources.name: Eleven v3 (alpha) announcement
sources.notes: Expressive TTS with inline audio tags ([whispers], [sighs], [excited]), a Text to Dialogue endpoint for multi-speaker turns and interruptions, 70+ languages. Not recommended for real-time or conversational use at launch (latency, reliability); v2.5 Turbo or Flash recommended for real time.

sources.name: Crowd Pathfinding and Steering Using Flow Field Tiles
sources.notes: Book and year from the hosting site and contributor knowledge. Supreme Commander 2: 10x10 m sectors linked by portals; A* over the portal graph; 8-bit cost field with 255 for walls; integration field from the goal; shared flow field directions for many units; dirty sectors rebuilt by a time-sliced queue; earlier per-unit repathing on collision compounded stalls.
sources.venue: Game AI Pro, ed. Steve Rabin, CRC Press (chapter 23)

sources.name: How to use the Machine Learning Deformer in Unreal Engine
sources.notes: ML Deformer learns morph-target corrections from offline muscle, flesh or cloth caches (Neural Morph, Nearest Neighbor models) to approximate them at runtime on the GPU; training caches can reach 50-100 GB.

sources.name: Motion Matching in Unreal Engine
sources.notes: Pose Search plugin; Motion Matching node selects poses from a database to match a runtime query without transition logic; brute force, PCAKDTree, VPTree search; Game Animation Sample; no learned networks described.

sources.name: Modeling Individual Personalities in The Sims 3
sources.notes: Distinct Sim personalities expressed through autonomous behavior; in-game visualization tools used to tune it; a fine-grained, data-driven social system in which non-programmers defined hundreds of interactions and thousands of production rules.

sources.name: Versu: A Simulationist Storytelling System
sources.notes: Social practices as reactive joint plans; agents score actions by simulating and undoing them against 300+ desires; exclusion logic; Praxis; 1,000+ parameterized actions; Facade comparison of 30 speech acts and 27 beats.
sources.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Intelligence and AI in Games 6(2)

sources.name: Pluribus: First AI to beat pros in 6-player poker
sources.notes: Blueprint by improved Monte Carlo CFR in 8 days on a 64-core server, under 512 GB RAM, no GPUs, under $150; play on two CPUs and under 128 GB; 1-33 s per decision (about 20 s per hand); about 5 bb/100 over 10,000 hands; leaf nodes choose among four continuation strategies.

sources.name: diplomacy_cicero
sources.notes: Code MIT (AGPL subdirectory), weights CC-BY-NC 4.0; planning agents DiL-piKL and bilateral correlated planning; training scripts assume a Slurm cluster (example 256 GPUs); archived read-only 2025-04-17.

sources.name: Crude oil
sources.notes: Oil field yield in percent; 1% equals 300 pumpjack cycles; yield floor of 20% (raised from 10% in 0.15.0).

sources.name: Electric system
sources.notes: Power is spread evenly so machines slow proportionally (300 kW load on 180 kW solar runs at 60%); producer priority solar, then steam/turbine/fusion, then accumulators; idle drain per machine.

sources.name: Enemies
sources.notes: Evolution factor rises with time, total pollution produced, and destroyed spawners (0.002 each by default), squashed as total/(1+total); enemies attack only when the pollution cloud reaches nests; absorbed pollution recruits units (small biter 4, behemoth biter 400); attack groups launch every 1 to 10 minutes.

sources.name: Logistic network
sources.notes: Roboports define logistic and construction zones; logistic robots move items between active provider, passive provider, storage, buffer, and requester chests in priority order; default cargo 1 item at 3 tiles/s; construction robots build blueprint ghosts, repair, and deconstruct.

sources.name: Pollution
sources.notes: Pollution stored per 32x32-tile chunk and updated every 64 ticks; chunks at 15 or more diffuse 2% to each cardinal neighbor; tiles absorb per chunk per minute (water 1.536, grass 1.10592); trees damaged above 60; spawners absorb pollution to send attack units (small biter 4); evolution driven by pollution produced.

sources.name: Rail signal
sources.notes: Rail signals divide track into blocks; a train reserves a block and the block's other entrance signals turn red; chain signals mirror the signal ahead so trains stop earlier; circuit conditions can force a signal red.

sources.name: Space Age
sources.notes: Paid expansion released 2024-10-21: planets Vulcanus, Fulgora, Gleba (agriculture whose produce spoils), and Aquilo (machines freeze without heating); space platforms carry cargo between planets and must shoot down asteroids; adds Quality, Elevated Rails, and the Recycler (75% loss).

sources.name: Transport belts/Physics
sources.notes: 4 items per lane per tile on straight belts; throughput 15, 30, 45, 60 items/s for transport, fast, express, and turbo belts.

authors: Meta Fundamental AI Research Diplomacy Team (FAIR)
sources.name: Human-level play in the game of Diplomacy by combining language models with strategic reasoning
sources.notes: Cicero: language model plus planning and RL; in 40 games of an anonymous online league it scored more than double the human average and ranked in the top 10% of participants who played more than one game.

sources.name: OMNI-EPIC: Open-endedness via Models of human Notions of Interestingness with Environments Programmed in Code
Harvest Moon (SNES) guide
sources.notes: Fan guide; publication date not stated, accessed revision. Two and a half years to restore the farm, father's final evaluation, five eligible wives, stamina and power berries subpage.

sources.name: Mapping Hearthstone Deck Spaces through MAP-Elites with Sliding Boundaries
Illuminating Mario Scenes in the Latent Space of a Generative Adversarial Network
Some notes on programming objects in The Sims
sources.notes: Objects hold behaviors whose advertisements state which of nine motives (energy, comfort, hunger, hygiene, bladder, room, social, fun, mood) they satisfy; values fixed or scaled by personality points in opposing pairs such as nice/grouchy; distance attenuation presets high, moderate, low, none; check trees hide unavailable interactions; Sims choose the behavior that maximizes happiness. Examples: toilet 0-70 Bladder, Feed Fish 1-11 Fun by Playful.
sources.venue: Qualitative Reasoning Group, Northwestern University (course notes)

sources.name: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
sources.notes: One-shot 3-4 bit weight quantization with approximate second-order information; 175B model quantized in about four GPU hours with minimal accuracy loss; about 3.25x (A100) and 4.5x (A6000) faster generation than FP16.

sources.name: Brax: A Differentiable Physics Engine for Large Scale Rigid Body Simulation
sources.notes: JAX rigid-body engine; millions of steps per second on one accelerator, hundreds of millions across accelerators; Ant locomotion in about ten seconds versus about half an hour for standard PPO.

sources.name: Change and Constant: Breaking Conventions with 'The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild'
sources.notes: GDC 2017 session by Nintendo's game director, art director, and technical director on how Breath of the Wild broke series conventions; the technical director presented the chemistry engine.

sources.name: Large Language Models and Games: A Survey and Roadmap
sources.notes: Nine roles: player, NPC, player assistant, commentator/reteller, analyst, game master, game mechanic, automated designer, design assistant. LLM GMs accommodate bizarre requests; NPCs may hallucinate quests; design-tool latency 30 s to over a minute; commentary and retelling research limited.

sources.name: Civilization IV's lead designer wants you to financially ruin your enemies
sources.notes: Soren Johnson names M.U.L.E. and Railroad Tycoon as inspirations; Steam Early Access launch set for 2015-02-12; matches of 30-40 minutes; hostile takeovers through share purchases.

sources.name: Rows of corn, lines of code: Swiss automation game The Farmer Was Replaced launches 10 October
sources.notes: 1.0 launch on 10 October 2025 after early access from 10 February 2023 with 150,000 copies sold; 1.0 adds multiple drones and a revamped tech tree; Zurich publisher Metaroot.

sources.name: Relaxing nature sim Equilinox is out and seems to be a hit with users
sources.notes: Development since 2015; 120+ species, 10 biome types spread by grasses, 60+ tasks; animals eat, reproduce, grow, die, hunt; a commenter notes evolution is triggered by meeting conditions rather than simulated selection.

sources.name: GDC 2025 State of the Game Industry: Devs weigh in on layoffs, AI, and more
sources.notes: Over 3,000 respondents (+/-2%). 52% work at companies that implemented generative AI; 36% personally use it; 30% think it is having a negative impact on the industry, up 12 points.

sources.name: GDC 2026 State of the Game Industry reveals impact of layoffs, generative AI, and more
sources.notes: Over 2,300 respondents. 36% use generative AI at work (30% at studios vs 58% at publishing, support, marketing). 52% see negative impact (30% in 2025, 18% the year before), 7% positive. Uses: research or brainstorming 81%, daily tasks 47%, code assistance 47%, prototyping 35%. ChatGPT 74%.

sources.name: Genesis World (formerly Genesis): a generative and universal physics engine for robotics and beyond
sources.notes: Apache-2.0; rigid, FEM, MPM, PBD, SPH solvers in one scene; academic project from Dec 2024, Genesis World 1.0 announced May 2026; no arXiv paper listed.

sources.name: JSONSchemaBench: A Rigorous Benchmark of Structured Outputs for Language Models
sources.notes: 10K real-world JSON schemas; evaluates Guidance, Outlines, llama.cpp, XGrammar, OpenAI, and Gemini on efficiency, constraint coverage, and output quality, plus the official JSON Schema Test Suite.

sources.name: Mathematical exploration and discovery at scale
sources.notes: AlphaEvolve applied to 67 problems in analysis, combinatorics, geometry and number theory; mostly rediscovers best known constructions, improves several, sometimes generalizes finite results to formulas.

sources.name: llama.cpp GBNF grammar guide (grammars/README.md)
sources.notes: GBNF production rules constrain local model output; a JSON Schema subset converts to GBNF via json_schema or response_format. Caveats: known grammar performance problems, many optional items make sampling slow, unsupported schema features (nested $ref, patternProperties, uniqueItems, conditionals) are skipped silently.

sources.name: Aurora (Giant Bomb wiki)
sources.notes: Release 2004, developer Steve Walmsley, PC, free to download. Turn-based science fiction 4X; time advances in steps from 5 seconds to 30 days; eleven Trans-Newtonian Elements with accessibility 0.1 to 1; jump points found by survey; colony cost from gravity, atmosphere, temperature, lowered by terraforming; ship classes designed from components; missiles versus beams; scientists, administrators, naval officers, ground commanders improve over time.

sources.name: Technical Challenges of Deploying Reinforcement Learning Agents for Game Testing in AAA Games
sources.notes: EA SEED added an experimental RL system to scripted-bot automated testing for titles including Battlefield 2042 and Dead Space (2023); reports the largest integration time sinks.

sources.name: Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for Procedural Content Generation
Improving Playtesting Coverage via Curiosity Driven Reinforcement Learning Agents
Creatures: Artificial Life Autonomous Software Agents for Home Entertainment
sources.notes: About 1,000 neurons in 9 lobes and 5,000 synapses; concept space of about 640 cells; 16-cell decision layer, strongest cell acts; drive reduction releases reward and drive increase releases punishment chemicals that reinforce synapses; 256 chemicals with gene-defined reactions; haploid genome of about 320 genes; crossover at gene boundaries with omission, duplication, and mutation; genes switch on at set ages.
sources.venue: University of Sussex Cognitive Science Research Paper CSRP434 (Millennium Technical Report 9601)

sources.name: Procedural Content Generation through Quality Diversity
Automatic Posterior Transformation for Likelihood-Free Inference
sources.notes: Sequential neural posterior estimation with arbitrary, dynamically updated proposals and normalizing-flow density estimators; works on high-dimensional time series and images.

sources.name: Richelieu: Self-Evolving LLM-Based Agents for AI Diplomacy
sources.notes: LLM Diplomacy agent combining planning with memory and reflection, goal-directed negotiation, and self-play memory augmentation without human data.

sources.name: Human-Like Playtesting with Deep Learning
sources.notes: King: CNN trained on player moves in Candy Crush Saga and Candy Crush Soda Saga predicts human moves and estimates level difficulty; correlates better with average difficulty than MCTS at a fraction of compute.
sources.venue: IEEE Conference on Computational Intelligence and Games (CIG 2018)

sources.name: First city-building videogame
sources.notes: Record states the first city-building videogame is generally considered to be Utopia, released on the Intellivision in 1981; the companion record for first simulation videogame also names Utopia by Don Daglow, 1981.

sources.name: WaveFunctionCollapse
sources.notes: Overlapping and simple tiled models; lowest-entropy observation plus propagation; README lists Bad North, Caves of Qud, Dead Static Drive, Townscaper, and Matrix Awakens, plus Unity, Unreal Engine 5, Godot 4, and Houdini adaptations.

sources.name: MineWorld: a Real-Time and Open-Source Interactive World Model on Minecraft
sources.notes: Visual-action autoregressive Transformer over image and action tokens with parallel decoding; 4 to 7 fps across model scales; code and model released (microsoft/MineWorld).

sources.name: Training Agents Inside of Scalable World Models
sources.notes: Dreamer 4 learns behavior by RL inside a world model trained mostly on unlabeled video; model runs interactively on one GPU; first agent to obtain Minecraft diamonds from offline data only.

sources.name: Mastering diverse control tasks through world models
sources.notes: DreamerV3: one fixed configuration beats specialized methods on over 150 tasks; first algorithm to collect Minecraft diamonds from scratch without human data or curricula (first diamond near 30M environment steps, about 17 days of play).

sources.name: Democracy 4: the fixed income rewrite
sources.notes: Democracy 1-4 use a homebrew neural network where voters, groups, policies, ministers, and events are neurons capped 0..1 or -1..+1; percentage effects on 0-1 income favored the rich; added fixed-income neurons that can exceed 1.

sources.name: A Formal Basis for the Heuristic Determination of Minimum Cost Paths
sources.notes: Introduces the A* search algorithm: nodes are expanded in order of path cost so far plus a heuristic estimate of remaining cost; with an admissible heuristic the first path found to the goal has minimum cost.
sources.venue: IEEE Transactions on Systems Science and Cybernetics 4(2), 100-107

sources.name: Matrix-Game 2.0: An Open-Source, Real-Time, and Streaming Interactive World Model
sources.notes: 25 fps on one H100 at 352x640; 1.3B base plus action modules (~1.8B); ~1,200 h from Unreal Engine, Minecraft, GTA driving, Temple Run, Sekai; Self-Forcing with DMD, 3 steps, rolling KV cache; weights and code released; no explicit memory.

sources.name: Hidden Door blog
sources.notes: Post list: Introducing Early Access (2025-08-13), Now Playing: Dracula (2025-10-15), Inside our agentic story harness (2026-10-02), A time-traveling narrative harness (2026-10-16). Post bodies not read.

sources.name: Hidden Door
sources.notes: Story engine turns player intent into story beats and world-state changes checked against canon and rules before display (example: Dracula cannot enter uninvited); typed, auditable world model with embeddings; nearly 100 specialized narrative tasks; a tuned 1.7B model beat a 120B general model on one core task. Licensed worlds include Dracula, Oz, Pride and Prejudice, Sherlock Holmes.

sources.name: Subspace Neural Physics: Fast Data-Driven Interactive Simulation
sources.notes: Ubisoft La Forge: network predicts dynamics in a PCA subspace of an offline cloth or deformable simulation; reported 300-5000x faster than the source simulation at small extra memory; not stated to have shipped.
sources.venue: ACM SIGGRAPH/Eurographics Symposium on Computer Animation 2019

sources.name: Machine Learning: Physics Simulation, Kolmogorov Complexity, and Squishy Bunnies
sources.notes: Ubisoft Montreal talk on learned interactive physics and cloth, approximately 300 to 5000 times faster than standard simulation; does not name a shipped title.

sources.name: Micropolis: open-source SimCity source code
sources.notes: GPL release of the original SimCity engine (year from contributor knowledge). micropolis-java engine: crimeScan sets cell crime = 128 - land value + population density (cap 300) minus a smoothed police map, clamped 0-250, high-crime message above an average of 100; doDisasters fires with chance 1/481, 1/241, or 1/61 per cycle by level, then picks fire, flood, tornado, earthquake, nothing, or a monster if average pollution exceeds 60.

sources.name: Factorio Learning Environment
sources.notes: Lab-play (eight structured tasks) and open-play (largest factory on a procedural map). LLM agents found strategies such as electric drilling but failed at complex automation such as electronic circuits; weak spatial reasoning and error recovery.

sources.name: DiffTaichi: Differentiable Programming for Physical Simulation
sources.notes: 10 differentiable simulators; elastic simulator 4.2x shorter than hand CUDA at similar speed and 188x faster than TensorFlow; controllers optimized in tens of iterations.

sources.name: Game Generation via Large Language Models
Versu
sources.notes: Community wiki; accessed revision. Little Text People acquired by Linden Lab in early 2012; project cancelled early 2014; Blood & Laurels later released independently on iPad.

sources.name: Decart and Etched release Oasis, a real-time AI-generated Minecraft-like world model
sources.notes: Oasis at 20 fps and 460p on H100s; 500M open weights described as scaled down; autoencoder with DiT layers, next-frame prediction; only a few minutes of play at a time; placing a dirt block can bring up an entirely new environment.

sources.name: Bringing the ER to VR: Surgeon Simulator: Experience Reality
sources.notes: VR edition by Bossa Studios on PlayStation VR (launch), HTC Vive 2016-12-05, Oculus Touch 2016-12-06.

sources.name: How Inworld helped an AI game with 20 million players reach profitability
sources.notes: Vendor case study of Death by AI (Playroom, six staff): 700,000 daily users three days after launch, 10 million players in month one, 20 million and 3 million play hours by month three; 1.2 billion tokens in month one; moved from GPT-3.5/GPT-4 and ElevenLabs to Inworld; claims of lower cost and latency are unverified.

sources.name: Cost is the wall in front of consumer AI. We are taking it down.
sources.notes: Vendor price list as of June 2026: Realtime TTS-2 about $10 per 1M characters at scale ($25 on demand), TTS-1.5 Mini about $5 at scale, speech-to-text about $0.10 per hour; ElevenLabs API cited at about $100 per 1M characters. Claims about 3 in 100 consumer AI users ever pay, paying users spend $5-20 per month.

sources.name: Inworld TTS-1.5: Upgrading the #1 Ranked TTS Model with Production-Grade Latency, Expression and Stability
sources.notes: TTS-1.5 Max: P90 time to first audio under 250 ms, $25 per 1M characters (about $0.025 per minute). TTS-1.5 Mini: under 130 ms, $15 per 1M characters (about $0.015 per minute). 15 languages. Vendor figures.

sources.name: Project Hospital: a realistic take on hospital simulation
sources.notes: Interview with Jan Benes, lead programmer at Oxymoron Games: examinations uncover symptoms and enough symptoms give a diagnosis; symptom frequency tuned so one exam rarely suffices; dangerous hidden symptoms must be found and treated in time; based on real medicine with input from professionals.

sources.name: Unity: A General Platform for Intelligent Agents
sources.notes: Introduces the open-source Unity ML-Agents Toolkit for training agents inside Unity environments.

sources.name: World and Human Action Models towards gameplay ideation
sources.notes: 23 authors (Microsoft Research, Ninja Theory, universities). Introduces WHAM; consistency, diversity, and persistency as capabilities for creative ideation.

sources.name: WaveFunctionCollapse is Constraint Solving in the Wild
sources.notes: Public release 2016-09-30; WFC as MRV-ordered search with arc-consistency propagation and global restarts; Caves of Qud and Proc Skater 2016 as early users; global constraints caused many conflicts that backtracking resolved.

sources.name: GPUDrive: Data-driven, multi-agent driving simulation at 1 million FPS
sources.notes: Built on Madrona; over one million simulation steps per second; multi-agent driving agents trained on Waymo Open Motion scenarios in minutes to hours.

sources.name: Genesis speeds up AI robot training with simulations 430,000x faster than reality
sources.notes: Reports the launch claim of up to 43 million FPS (430,000x real time) for simple scenes; notes skepticism and that contact-rich dexterous scenes remain hard.

sources.name: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering
sources.notes: Anisotropic 3D Gaussians from SfM points, interleaved optimization and density control, visibility-aware tile rasterizer; real-time (>=30 fps) novel-view synthesis at 1080p.

sources.name: A Contribution to the Mathematical Theory of Epidemics
sources.notes: Introduces the compartment model of epidemics; shows that for each epidemic there is a threshold population density, set by infectivity, recovery, and death rates, below which introducing infection does not produce an epidemic.
sources.venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society of London, Series A, 115(772):700-721

sources.name: PCGRL: Procedural Content Generation via Reinforcement Learning
Khronos releases KHR_gaussian_splatting glTF extension release candidate
sources.notes: Release candidate of baseline glTF 2.0 splat extension; compression proposals SPZ (Niantic Spatial) and L-GSC (Qualcomm); contributors Autodesk, Cesium/Bentley, Esri, Huawei, Niantic Spatial, NVIDIA, XGRIDS; ratification expected Q2 2026.

sources.name: Bandit Based Monte-Carlo Planning
sources.notes: Introduces UCT, applying the UCB1 bandit rule to node selection in Monte Carlo tree search.

sources.name: KRAFTON Introduces PUBG Ally Beta Test
sources.notes: Ally Duo arcade mode on Sanhok, 17 June to 1 July 2026; AI companion Ella powered by an on-device small language model built on NVIDIA ACE with speech-to-text and text-to-speech; fast actions (movement, item collection) with minimal latency, strategy from game context and conversation; Korean, Chinese, English.

sources.name: Automating the Search for Artificial Life with Foundation Models
sources.notes: ASAL: vision-language foundation model scores rendered simulations to search Boids, Particle Life, Game of Life, Lenia and NCA rule spaces for target phenomena, open-ended novelty, or diverse illumination.

sources.name: GraphCast: Learning skillful medium-range global weather forecasting
sources.notes: 0.25 degree global, 10-day forecasts in under one minute; better than the top operational deterministic system on 90% of 1,380 verification targets.

sources.name: ShinkaEvolve: Towards Open-Ended And Sample-Efficient Program Evolution
sources.notes: Open-source LLM program evolution; new state-of-the-art circle packing with about 150 samples versus thousands for earlier systems.

sources.name: NVIDIA, Disney and Google contribute open-source Newton engine to the Linux Foundation
sources.notes: Newton robotics physics engine built on NVIDIA Warp and OpenUSD with MuJoCo compatibility; co-developed with Google DeepMind and Disney Research.

sources.name: Mean field games
sources.notes: Founding MFG paper: many rational players each optimize against the aggregate distribution; coupled forward-backward nonlinear PDEs shown well-posed.

sources.name: Learning in Mean Field Games: A Survey
sources.notes: Survey of RL and iterative best-response or policy-evaluation methods for static, stationary and evolutive MFG equilibria and social optima.

sources.name: Fourier Neural Operator for Parametric Partial Differential Equations
sources.notes: Neural operator with kernels parameterized in Fourier space; Burgers, Darcy, Navier-Stokes; up to three orders of magnitude faster than traditional PDE solvers; zero-shot super-resolution.

sources.name: Hunyuan-GameCraft: High-dynamic Interactive Game Video Generation with Hybrid History Condition
sources.notes: Over 1M recordings from 100+ AAA titles split into 6 s clips; keyboard and mouse unified into camera actions with Plucker embeddings; hybrid history conditioning; PCM distillation 0.25 to 6.6 fps, under 5 s latency per action; 720p; lacks shooting and throwing actions.

sources.name: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration
sources.notes: 4-bit weight-only quantization protecting about 1% salient weights chosen from activation statistics; TinyChat runtime over 3x faster than Hugging Face FP16 on desktop and mobile GPUs.

sources.name: Can Centaur truly simulate human cognition? The fundamental limitation of instruction understanding
sources.notes: With task instructions removed or replaced by misleading ones, Centaur still generally outperformed domain-specific cognitive models; authors conclude it relies on superficial statistical cues rather than understanding instructions.

sources.name: The untapped potential of virtual game worlds to shed light on real world epidemics
sources.notes: Read via secondary summaries (Medical News Today, Wikipedia). Uses the World of Warcraft Corrupted Blood outbreak to argue virtual worlds capture individual behavior in epidemics; players entered quarantine zones and assumed contact would not infect them; quarantine failed and the developer reset servers.

sources.name: Condition
sources.notes: Condition drains per hour while a need is empty: warmth 20%, fatigue 1%, hunger 1%, thirst 2%; passive regeneration about 1% per hour when all needs are above zero; afflictions drain or cap condition.

sources.name: Madrona: a prototype engine for high-throughput batch simulation
sources.notes: MIT license; GPU batch ECS, XPBD rigid bodies, batch renderer; archetypes fixed up front; example ports include Escape Room, Overcooked-AI, Hide and Seek, Hanabi; research code with breaking APIs.

sources.name: Decart Unveils Real-Time AI Game Engine, Raises $21M to Make AI-Generated Worlds More Affordable
sources.notes: Oasis served on Nvidia H100s; article states cost remains a significant barrier to deploying such models at scale; Etched claims its Sohu chip would serve ten times more users at the same cost. No per-hour cost given.

sources.name: Isaac Gym: High Performance GPU-Based Physics Simulation For Robot Learning
sources.notes: Physics simulation and policy training both on one GPU; reports 2-3 orders of magnitude faster training than CPU-simulator pipelines.

sources.name: Natural Language Understanding in Facade: Surface-text Processing
sources.notes: Venue and year from the hosted file name and contributor knowledge. Forward-chaining template rules map surface text to 24 discourse act types including a catch-all for non-understanding; about 800 template rules compile to about 6,800 Jess rules; permissive rules accept false positives to reduce non-understanding; under 300 ms on a 2 GHz machine.
sources.venue: TIDSE 2004 (Technologies for Interactive Digital Storytelling and Entertainment)

sources.name: Craftax: A Lightning-Fast Benchmark for Open-Ended Reinforcement Learning
sources.notes: JAX rewrite of the Crafter survival-crafting game; up to 250x faster than the Python original; PPO for 1 billion interactions in under an hour on one GPU.

sources.name: The Prom: An Example of Socially-Oriented Gameplay
sources.notes: Precursor design of Prom Week on CiF: characters with traits, interests, statuses, and networks of liking, attraction, and respect; social games modify social state; level goals made of social states.
sources.venue: Proceedings of the Sixth AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Interactive Digital Entertainment (AIIDE)

sources.name: Prom Week
sources.notes: Demo paper: Prom Week uses the social AI system Comme il Faut (CiF) to make social relationships playable.
sources.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Interactive Digital Entertainment (AIIDE) 9(1)

sources.name: Social Story Worlds With Comme il Faut
sources.notes: Social exchanges with one intent, preconditions, initiator and responder influence rule sets, and accept and reject instantiations; buddy, romance, and cool networks; Prom Week has 34 statuses, 44 traits, 3 relationships, and over 5,000 influence rules; social facts database treats events as known to all; volition from summed rule weights.
sources.venue: IEEE Transactions on Computational Intelligence and AI in Games 6(2)

sources.name: CICERO
sources.notes: Describes a controllable dialogue model steered by plans from a planning engine that predicts other players' moves from the board and conversation history; games played on webDiplomacy.net.

sources.name: Introducing V-JEPA 2 world model and new physical reasoning benchmarks
sources.notes: 1.2B parameters; IntPhys 2, MVPBench, CausalVQA released; humans 85-95% on the benchmarks; current video models near chance on IntPhys 2; single time-scale limitation.

sources.name: An Aurora, Sharpened in the Key of C
sources.notes: Community weblog post (not journalism) dated 2020-04-13 announcing that Aurora had just been released in a version ported to a new language; comments identify it as the C# rewrite of the Visual Basic 6 original, which still works but is no longer updated.

sources.name: Introducing Muse: Our first generative AI model designed for gameplay ideation
sources.notes: Trained on over 1 billion images and controller actions (over 7 years of play) from Bleeding Edge under EULA; 300x180; WHAM-1.6B and WHAM-206M; weights, sample data, and WHAM Demonstrator released on Azure AI Foundry.

sources.name: TRELLIS.2 repository
sources.notes: 4B-parameter image-to-3D model with O-Voxel sparse structure; PBR GLB output (base color, roughness, metallic, opacity); 512^3 to 1536^3; ~3 s, ~17 s, ~60 s on H100; MIT license.

sources.name: WHAMM real-time Quake II world model (Microsoft Research blog)
sources.notes: WHAMM: MaskGIT-style 500M backbone plus 250M refiner; 10+ fps at 640x360 vs ~1 fps for WHAM-1.6B; one week of Quake II training data; one part of one level; limits: blurry enemies, wrong damage, 0.9 s context, unreliable health counters.

sources.name: Mindustry Logic: Introduction
sources.notes: Mindustry Logic (mlog) was added in v6; it is assembly-like with one operation per instruction and can control buildings and turrets, read and write memory cells, and read switch input.

sources.name: Differentiable Logic Cellular Automata: From Game of Life to Pattern Generation
sources.notes: Learned binary logic-gate circuits as NCA rules; learns Game of Life from all 512 3x3 configurations with 336 active gates; lizard pattern 577 gates; self-healing and asynchronous variants.

sources.name: Bitburner
sources.notes: Programming-based incremental RPG with contributions from hundreds of developers and five years of development before Steam; lists Else Heart.break(), Hacknet, Uplink, and Deus Ex as inspirations.

sources.name: DeepStack: Expert-level artificial intelligence in heads-up no-limit poker
sources.notes: Recursive reasoning with decomposition and a learned value function; beat professionals with statistical significance over 44,000 hands of heads-up no-limit hold'em.

sources.name: Growing Neural Cellular Automata
sources.notes: 16-channel cells, fixed Sobel perception, shared ~8K-parameter update network, stochastic asynchronous updates, alive masking; regenerating variants regrow damaged shapes.

sources.name: Texture Generation with Neural Cellular Automata
sources.notes: NCA textures with fewer than 10K parameters (5,868 in the reported model); interactive real-time WebGL demo.

sources.name: Illuminating search spaces by mapping elites
Word2World: Generating Stories and Worlds through Large Language Models
Stalk Market
sources.notes: Community wiki; accessed revision. New Horizons turnips: Daisy Mae sells Sunday mornings, prices change twice daily under one of four weekly patterns, turnips spoil the following Sunday.

sources.name: AlphaEvolve: A coding agent for scientific and algorithmic discovery
sources.notes: Evolutionary pipeline of LLMs editing whole code files with feedback from automated evaluators; provably correct improvements in math and computer science problems.

sources.name: Warp Speed: NVIDIA Open-Source Framework Accelerates Scientific Computing in Python
sources.notes: Warp writes differentiable GPU kernels in Python; Warp 1.5 tile programming; Autodesk reports fluid sims 8x faster and 5x larger.

sources.name: NVIDIA ACE autonomous game characters: PUBG Ally, inZOI Smart Zoi, NARAKA AI teammate
sources.notes: PUBG Ally on Mistral-Nemo-Minitron-8B; inZOI Smart Zoi with on-device LM; NARAKA: BLADEPOINT mobile PC AI teammate with local inference (2025-03); MIR5 adaptive bosses; AI People; Dead Meat; Audio2Face in Alien: Rogue Incursion.

sources.name: Cosmos World Foundation Model Platform for Physical AI
sources.notes: ~20M hours raw video to ~100M clips; diffusion (Text2World, Video2World) and autoregressive WFMs; causal tokenizers (continuous 16-dim, discrete FSQ 64K vocab); open weights, permissive licenses; github nvidia-cosmos.

sources.name: NVIDIA DLSS 4 Introduces Multi Frame Generation and Transformer-Based AI Models
sources.notes: Multi Frame Generation up to 3 extra frames per rendered frame on RTX 50; transformer models for Ray Reconstruction, Super Resolution, DLAA; 75 games and apps at launch; up to 8x vs brute force; Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 named as following.

sources.name: Gamescom 2025: DLSS 4 and RTX game announcements
sources.notes: August 2025 Smart ZOI update: better observation of surroundings and reaction to events, actions better match inner thoughts. The Oversight Bureau launches with on-device Riva ASR (English, streaming, word boosting); a narrative engine uses one model to analyze the transcript and another to decide dialogue and behavior.

sources.name: NVIDIA RTX Neural Rendering Introduces Next Era of AI-Powered Graphics Innovation
sources.notes: RTX Neural Shaders; Neural Texture Compression up to 7x VRAM saving vs block compression; Neural Materials up to 5x faster; Neural Radiance Cache in RTX GI SDK; RTX Neural Faces; Mega Geometry; DirectX cooperative vectors announced.

sources.name: NVIDIA ACE for Games
sources.notes: Total War: PHARAOH AI advisor on a small on-device model connected to game data; Smart Zois plan, act, reflect; PUBG co-player characters; MIR5 bosses adapt to tactics. On-device models listed: Nemotron 3 Nano 4B and 9B, Nemotron ASR 140M and 600M, Chatterbox and Qwen 3 TTS, Audio2Face-3D. NVIGI runs in-process with CUDA in Graphics scheduling.

sources.name: NVIDIA Cosmos
sources.notes: Cosmos 3 omni family: Super 64B, Nano 16B, Edge 4B; OpenMDW1.1 license; uses: synthetic data for AV and robots, world simulator for closed-loop evaluation, robot policy post-training; no mention of games.

sources.name: NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 Delivers Major Upgrade With 2nd Gen Transformer Model For Super Resolution and 6X Dynamic Multi Frame Generation
sources.notes: 2nd generation transformer SR for all RTX GPUs; Dynamic MFG and 6X mode (up to five generated frames) for RTX 50; over 250 MFG titles; over 400 DLSS SR games and apps.

sources.name: NVIDIA DLSS 5 Available September 3rd: 3D-Guided Neural Rendering Debuts In NBA 2K27
sources.notes: Final neural rendering stage trained on color, albedo, lighting, normals; input color and motion vectors; deterministic output; Structure and Tone Intensity, semantic and engine masking; RTX 50 and GeForce NOW; NBA 2K27 first title; 5x speedup since March.

sources.name: NVIGI-Core: NVIDIA In-Game Inferencing SDK core
sources.notes: Requires RTX 30x0 or A6000 class GPU or newer (4080/4090/5080/5090 preferred), at least 8 GB VRAM with 12 GB recommended, Windows 11 22H2; some plugins require RTX 40x0; ARM64 (RTX Spark) is a developer preview.

sources.name: Bitburner documentation (community fork)
sources.notes: Fork of the official documentation: hack, grow, and weaken with a security floor of max(1, round(start/3)); augmentations bought from factions with reputation, each purchase doubles later prices, installing resets most progress; BitNodes destroyed via w0r1d_d43m0n at hacking 3000 grant Source-Files; stock forecasts.

sources.name: Introducing Odyssey-2: A General-Purpose World Model
sources.notes: Every frame generated in under 50 ms (~20 fps); text-prompt interaction; multi-minute streams; causal autoregressive; API announced as coming soon.

sources.name: Germs
sources.notes: Five germ types; germs live on tiles, items, buildings, gases, and liquids; per-germ exposure thresholds; inhalation and ingestion exposure tiers; contraction chance 0.5 - 0.5 x tanh(resistance / 4); heat, chlorine, and radiation kill germs.

sources.name: Liquid Pipe
sources.notes: Each segment holds 10 kg; packets move once per second; max 10 kg/s per line; liquid exchanges heat with the pipe segment and its tile.

sources.name: Morale
sources.notes: Morale from timed buffs (Mess Hall +3, Banquet Hall +6, Private Bedroom +3; food up to +16; decor up to +12); expectation rises with skills learned; each point under adds 2.5% stress per cycle up to 25%; 2 or more over reduces stress 20% per cycle; overjoyed responses from 8 points over.

sources.name: Natural Gas Generator
sources.notes: Consumes 90 g/s natural gas; produces 800 W, 67.5 g/s polluted water, and 22.5 g/s carbon dioxide.

sources.name: Introducing the Realtime API
sources.notes: Speech-to-speech over a persistent WebSocket with GPT-4o (gpt-4o-realtime-preview), automatic interruption handling, function calling. Audio $100 and $200 per 1M input and output tokens, about $0.06 per minute in and $0.24 per minute out; text $5 and $20. Later updates through general availability in August 2025.

sources.name: Introducing Structured Outputs in the API
sources.notes: JSON Schema converted to a CFG; invalid tokens masked each step; gpt-4o-2024-08-06 scored 100% on complex schema following vs under 40% for gpt-4-0613. Limits: JSON Schema subset; first request with a new schema adds latency (under 10 s, up to a minute); max_tokens can still break output; values can be wrong.

sources.name: Introducing gpt-realtime
sources.notes: gpt-realtime: Big Bench Audio 82.8% vs 65.6%, MultiChallenge 30.5% vs 20.6%, ComplexFuncBench 66.5% vs 49.7% versus the December 2024 model; audio $32 per 1M input ($0.40 cached) and $64 per 1M output, 20% below gpt-4o-realtime-preview.

sources.name: OpenRCT2 source: Guest.cpp (guest ride choice and thoughts)
sources.notes: GPL-3.0 reimplementation of RollerCoaster Tycoon 2. Guests reject rides below minimum or above maximum preferred intensity (both widened by happiness), above nausea tolerance (300, 600, 800, 1000 plus happiness), or priced above twice value (value quartered in pay-to-enter parks); rejections create thoughts and lower happiness; guests with no ride left head home.

sources.name: OpenRCT2 source: Ride.cpp (ride reliability, inspection, and breakdowns)
sources.notes: GPL-3.0 reimplementation of RollerCoaster Tycoon 2. Reliability starts at 100% and drops every 256 ticks by the ride's unreliability factor plus an age penalty (one-eighth of it in year 1 up to double after 8 years); breakdown chance rises with reliability lost; weighted breakdown types, brake failure more likely in rain; inspection interval set by the player; repair restores reliability in proportion to its deficit.

sources.name: Ride rating calculation
sources.notes: Ride-independent excitement, intensity, and nausea terms from max positive, negative, and lateral g, drops (excitement capped at 9), highest drop, inversions (capped at 6), and scenery within 5 tiles of the station (0.05 each, max 47); excitement cut 25% above intensity 10 with further steps at 11, 12, 13.2, 14.5; lateral g penalties at 2.8 and 3.1. Page notes it is incomplete.

sources.name: Why we recommend Path Signals
sources.notes: Block signals reserve whole blocks, path signals reserve only track pieces on the route; block signals were the only type in the original game; OpenTTD 12 shows only path signal types by default.

sources.name: Manual/Orders
sources.notes: Go-to orders, full load any or all cargo, unload, transfer with partial payment for feeders, no loading, go via, timetables, conditional order jumps, shared orders, depot service orders.

sources.name: Manual/Signals
sources.notes: A block is all track reachable up to the next signal; path signals are red by default until a route is reserved; one-way path signals; entry pre-signals require a green exit.

sources.name: Not Even Wrong: On the Limits of Prediction as Explanation in Cognitive Science
sources.notes: Response to Centaur (Binz et al. 2025) arguing it moves toward a unified model of behavior without cognition rather than a unified theory of cognition.

sources.name: Thermal Conductivity
sources.notes: Tick 0.2 s; cell-to-cell q = dT x dt x k x 1000, x25 solid-gas, x625 liquid-liquid; no transfer below 1 C or 0.1 DTU; per-tick change capped at a quarter of the difference; insulated tile conductivity divided by (255/2)^2; building and pipe formulas.

sources.name: Tire and Vehicle Dynamics (3rd edition)
sources.notes: Standard reference on tire mechanics and the semi-empirical Magic Formula tire model. Publisher page confirms title, edition, date, and ISBN; formula content is from the book's common use, not the store page.

sources.name: Stellaris Dev Diary #11: Research & Technology
sources.notes: Three research areas (physics, society, engineering) each led by a scientist; each project choice draws three semi-random options weighted by ethics, scientist traits, and known techs; rare techs; special tech cards from anomalies and debris; procedurally generated improvement techs for long games.

sources.name: Stellaris Dev Diary #21: Administrative Sectors
sources.notes: Core-world limit with penalties beyond it; sectors with AI governors that develop planets and build mining stations; player sets sector capital, membership, focus, resource transfers, and taxation. Month inferred from image filenames dated 2016-02-15.

sources.name: Victoria 3 Dev Diary #6: Interest Groups
sources.notes: Political strength from pop wealth and enfranchisement; clout as share of national total; powerful, influential, marginalized classes; approval from laws, government membership, loyalists and radicals; traits activated by approval and clout.

sources.name: Victoria 3 Dev Diary #9: National Markets
sources.notes: Base price per good; buy orders from consumption and sell orders from production set market price; market access from infrastructure scales orders and blends local and market prices.

sources.name: Victoria 3 Dev Diary #54: Trade Revisions
sources.notes: Routes start at level 1 and grow or shrink weekly by profitability; midpoint purchase and sale prices; per-unit tariffs on base price; convoys; per-route bureaucracy cost replaces route cap; trade agreements and embargoes.

sources.name: Cities: Skylines II Feature Highlight #2: Traffic AI
sources.notes: Pathfinding cost combines time, comfort, money, and behavior; vehicles spread across lanes; parking fees enter route cost; citizens compare driving, transit, and walking; accident checks per road segment.

sources.name: Victoria 3 Dev Diary #80: Law Enactment and Revolution Clock in 1.3
sources.notes: Three enactment phases with success, advance, debate, and stall chances from interest-group endorsement; up to three setbacks; two-year cancellation cooldown; government petitions; revolution clock for revolutionary movements; 40 revolution events.

sources.name: Victoria 3 Dev Diary #74 - UX Improvements
sources.notes: UX changes: repositioned tooltips so players can move into a nested tooltip without opening another by accident; military tooltips break down battle calculations; more detailed pop needs, market access, and radicals tooltips. No date shown on the page; year inferred from screenshot timestamps (early 2023).

sources.name: Event modding (Crusader Kings III)
sources.notes: Events do not fire automatically; they are called from on_actions, decisions, or interactions. Structure: trigger, immediate, options with ai_chance, after. on_actions fire events, weighted random_events, or first_valid; trigger_event schedules follow-ups with random day delays; warns against every_living_character in pulse on_actions.

sources.name: Opinion
sources.notes: Most opinion decays to 0; Tyranny decays 0.25 per month; diplomacy +1 per point; same dynasty +5; faith hostility 0 to -30; attraction such as Beautiful +30, Ugly -20; Friend +60, Best Friend +120, Rival -60, Nemesis -120; Broke Truce -50 for 3 years; predecessor opinion is the only inheritable opinion.

sources.name: Succession
sources.notes: Primogeniture, ultimogeniture, and house seniority; confederate, regular, and high partition; elective title laws for feudal governments; the player continues as the player heir, normally the primary heir; with no valid heir, titles pass to the liege, or to a vassal for independent rulers.

sources.name: Traits
sources.notes: Characters tend to have no more than 3 personality traits; children gain them through events at ages 9, 11, and 13, more likely matching their guardian's; opposing traits are excluded; stress breaks at level 2 or higher can change traits.

sources.name: Diplomacy
sources.notes: Opinion capped at +200 and -200 with reasons shown in tooltips; each point of diplomatic reputation adds +5 to alliance acceptance and +3 to vassalization; base cap of 4 diplomatic relations, 1 diplomatic power per month per relation over cap; 2 diplomats.

authors: Hearts of Iron IV Wiki contributors
sources.name: Supply
sources.notes: Hub capacity via railway to capital, 15 to 35 by railway level, limited by weakest link; falloff per province from hub; trucks for motorized hubs; attrition at 35% supply or less; stored supply base cap 150%.
sources.venue: Hearts of Iron IV Wiki (Paradox Wikis)

sources.name: Regime
sources.notes: Hourly schedule per risk category, unlocked by hiring a Warden; Lockup, Sleep, Eat, Yard, Shower, Free Time, and Work variants; regimes confine prisoners to areas rather than forcing actions; cooks start four hours before Eat; prisoners never sleep from 8 AM to 8 PM.

sources.name: Education
sources.notes: Uneducated, educated, well educated, highly educated; elementary 300, high school 1,000, university 4,500 capacity; jobs have education requirements; higher-level buildings need more educated workers; citizens take lower jobs when nothing else is available; budget 50-150%; educated citizens make less garbage; page verified for version 1.16.

sources.name: Pops
sources.notes: Pops share profession, culture, religion, state, and workplace; professions grouped into classes and strata; standard of living sets needs and radicalism; monthly qualifications from literacy and wealth; literacy moves toward education access; migration toward states with higher attraction, mainly standard of living; workforce 25% by default.

sources.name: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
sources.notes: 25 agents in Smallville (Phaser, inspired by The Sims); gpt-3.5-turbo; memory stream retrieval by recency (0.995 per game hour), importance (1-10), relevance; reflection at importance sum 150; hierarchical planning; party awareness 1 to 13 agents, candidacy 1 to 8, network density 0.167 to 0.74 over two game days; cost thousands of dollars.
sources.venue: UIST '23 (ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology)

sources.name: joonspk-research/generative_agents
sources.notes: Apache-2.0 code for the paper; reverie backend simulation server plus Django frontend rendering Smallville; one game step is 10 game seconds; requires an OpenAI API key; replay and demo modes.

sources.name: Generative Agent Simulations of 1,000 People
sources.notes: Agents from two-hour interviews with 1,052 U.S. participants. The arXiv abstract as fetched (later version, retitled LLM Agents Grounded in Self-Reports Enable General-Purpose Simulation of Individuals) gives normalized GSS accuracy of 83% interview-only, 82% survey-only, 86% combined, 74% demographics-only; the Stanford HAI brief reports 85%. Reduced accuracy disparities across racial and ideological groups.

sources.name: Victoria 3 nested tooltip system
sources.notes: Reports that Victoria 3 adopts the nested tooltip system introduced in Crusader Kings III, where highlighted terms inside a tooltip open further tooltips. Title paraphrased from the page; year inferred from the article saying Victoria 3 was expected that year.

sources.name: Against the Storm
sources.notes: Early access on the Epic Games Store 2021-12-16; Steam and GOG early access 2022-11-01; full release 2023-12-08. Wikipedia gives October 2021 for early access; both agree on 2021.

sources.name: Cities: Skylines II
sources.notes: Video settings list DLSS 2.0 and FSR 1.0 upscaling; no dates given.

sources.name: Microsoft Flight Simulator (2020)
sources.notes: Video settings list DLSS 2.0 upscaling, DLSS Frame Generation support, and FSR 2.1; no dates given.

sources.name: Player-Driven Emergence in LLM-Driven Game Narrative
sources.notes: Dejaboom! TextWorld mystery with five GPT-4 NPCs holding backstories, clues, and ordered goals; 28 players; GPT-4 turned logs into narrative graphs; 53 emergent nodes (43 unique) vs designer graph. About 15 s lag frustrated 40%; NPC forgetting 10%; repetition 10%.

sources.name: An Image Synthesizer
sources.notes: Introduces gradient noise (Perlin noise), the basis of most noise-driven terrain heightmaps.

sources.name: Scaling up Mean Field Games with Online Mirror Descent
sources.notes: Online mirror descent converges to MFG Nash equilibrium under monotonicity; faster than fictitious play; solves MFGs with hundreds of billions of states.

sources.name: Mastering the game of Stratego with model-free multiagent reinforcement learning
sources.notes: DeepNash: Regularised Nash Dynamics (R-NaD), model-free, no search; top-3 2022 and all-time ranking on the Gravon Stratego platform against human experts.

sources.name: Learning Mesh-Based Simulation with Graph Networks
sources.notes: MeshGraphNets: message passing on simulation meshes with adaptive remeshing; cloth, aerodynamics, structural mechanics; 1-2 orders of magnitude faster than the training simulator.

sources.name: AgentSociety: Large-Scale Simulation of LLM-Driven Generative Agents Advances Understanding of Human Behaviors and Society
sources.notes: Over 10k agents and about 5 million interactions; agents with profiles, emotion, needs, and cognition layers; urban, social, and economic spaces (firms, banks, government); Ray actors, asyncio, MQTT bus; DeepSeek API chosen to avoid rate limits. Experiments on polarization, inflammatory messages, universal basic income, hurricane shock.
